Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verse 1:

(p-4821) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat al-Ahzab (The Confederates)

It is named thus because its story is a miracle for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), containing his victory through the wind and the angels, such that God sufficed the believers in fighting. It also distinguishes between the believers and the hypocrites through them. This is among the greatest objectives of the Qur'an. So said al-Mahayimi.

It is Medinan. Its verses number seventy-three. Imam Ahmad narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I have seen it, and it equals Surat al-Baqarah. We used to recite in it: 'The married man and the married woman, if they commit adultery, stone them outright as a punishment from God, and God is Mighty and Wise.'"

Ibn Kathir said: "This implies that there was once a Qur'an in it which was then abrogated, both its wording and its ruling."

And God knows best. End of quotation.

I say: This implication would be valid were this report sound. But since the compilers of the authentic collections did not include it, it is very weak.

(p-4822) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[1] ﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾ He, God's blessings be upon him, was addressed by his attribute rather than his name, in glorification of him. In the mode of direct address, one turns away from calling by name, to honor the one addressed; this is not so in the mode of reporting, where the name may be stated explicitly, and the glorification remains, as in the verse: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾ [al-Fath: 29], to teach people that he is the Messenger of God, and to instruct them to name him thus and to call him by it. His command, peace be upon him, to be God-fearing is for the exaltation and glorification of God-fearing (taqwa) itself, since even one like him is commanded to it; for its degrees have no end, while the intended aim is persistence and steadfastness in it. He did not make the command apply to his community as in its parallels, because the context that follows concerns a matter specific to him, such as the story of Zayd, may God be pleased with him. ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ meaning: do not agree with them on any matter, do not accept from them any opinion or counsel, keep away from them and be on your guard against them, for they are the enemies of God and the enemies of the believers, desiring only harm and opposition. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ meaning: He is more deserving that His commands be followed and obeyed, for He is the Knower of the outcomes of affairs and of the benefits as distinct from the harms, and the Wise who does nothing and commands nothing except by the motive of wisdom.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verses 2–4:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2–4] ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ (p-4823) ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 3] ﴿Allah has not made for a man two hearts within his chest. And He has not made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying by your mouths. But Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4]

﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾, i.e., in abandoning obedience to the disbelievers and the hypocrites and other than that: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 3], i.e., ascribe your affair to Him, and entrust it to His management, for He is sufficient as a Guardian to whom every matter is entrusted. ﴿Allah has not made for a man two hearts within his chest. And He has not made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4]. Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, Allah has not joined two hearts in one chest, nor marital relation and motherhood in one woman, nor sonship and adoption in one man. The meaning is: just as Allah, glorified is He, in His wisdom did not see fit to make for a human two hearts, because either He would do with one of them the same as He does with the other of the actions of the hearts, in which case one of them would be superfluous and not needed; or He would do with this one other than what He does with that one, and that would lead to the description of the one entity as being both willing and unwilling, knowing and suspecting, certain and doubting, in one state. Likewise, He did not see fit that one woman be both a mother to a man and his wife, because the mother is served, with the wing of humility lowered for her, while the wife is employed and disposed of through lying with her and otherwise, like a slave woman. These are two mutually contradictory states.

And that one man be an adopted son of a man and also his son, because sonship is the原 root of lineage and its nobility, while adoption is a superficial attachment by naming alone; and it is not possible for one thing to be both genuine and not genuine. This is an example that Allah set forth concerning Zayd ibn Harithah, a man of the tribe of Kalb who was taken captive as a child. The Arabs in their pre-Islamic time would raid and capture one another. Hakim ibn Hizam bought him for his aunt Khadijah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her, she gifted him to him. His father and uncle sought him, and he was given the choice, so he chose the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he freed him. They used to say: "Zayd ibn Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse, and His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40].

The indefinite form in "rajul" (a man), and the insertion of "min" (from) of comprehensiveness before "qalbayn" (two hearts), are two emphases for the intended meaning, as if He said: Allah has not made for the race of men, nor for any one of them, two hearts at all within his chest.

The benefit of mentioning "al-jawf" (the chest) is like the benefit in His saying: ﴿the hearts which are in the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. It is the increase in the hearer's conception and the clarity of what is indicated, for when he hears of it, he forms in his mind a chest containing two hearts, and so he is quicker to deny it.

The meaning of "zahara min imra'atihi" (he made zihar from his wife) is that he says to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." Zihar was a divorce among the people of pre-Islamic ignorance, so they would avoid the wife subjected to zihar just as they avoid a divorced woman. In Islam, it entails divorce and prohibition until the expiation (kaffarah) is paid.

Al-Azhari said: They specified "the back" (al-zahr) because it is the place of riding, and a woman is ridden when she is mounted sexually, so this is an allusive metonymy (kinayah talwihiyyah): it moves from the back to the thing ridden, and from that to the one covered. The meaning is: you are forbidden to me, you are not to be ridden as the mother is not ridden. Thus in al-Kashshaf.

His exalted saying: ﴿That﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4] refers to all that has been mentioned; that is, the fact that no one has two hearts, that wives are not mothers, and adopted sons are not sons; or it refers only to the last, namely the adoption: ﴿is your saying by your mouths﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4], i.e., it has no reality, so your claim does not entail that he be a genuine son; for he was created from the loins of another man, so it is not possible for him to have two fathers, just as it is not possible for one human to have two hearts. ﴿But Allah says the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4], i.e., that which is established and verified in reality. ﴿And He guides to the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4], i.e., the way of truth.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[5] ﴿Call them by their fathers' names; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients (mawali). And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts intended. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Call them by their fathers' names﴾, i.e., attribute them to their fathers. This is a singling out of the intended meaning among His true statements: ﴿that is more just in the sight of God﴾, i.e., more equitable and more wise. Ibn Kathir said: This command abrogates (naskh, cancellation of an earlier ruling) what was in the beginning of Islam, namely the permission to claim foreign sons, who were the adopted sons (adi'iya'). So God, blessed and exalted, commanded that their lineage be returned to their true fathers, and that this is justice, equity and righteousness. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Umar, who said: Zayd ibn Harithah, may God be pleased with him, the client (mawla) of the Messenger of God ﷺ, we would not call him except "Zayd ibn Muhammad", until the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Call them by their fathers' names; that is more just in the sight of God﴾. Muslim and others also narrated it.

They used to treat them in every respect as sons, including being alone with unmarriageable kin (al-mahārim) and otherwise. For this reason, Sahlah bint Suhayl, the wife of Abu Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with her, said: "O Messenger of God! We call Salim a son, and God has revealed what He has revealed, and he used to enter upon me, and I find in the soul of Abu Hudhayfah something because of that." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Nurse him, and he will become unlawful to you..." The hadith. For this reason, when this ruling was abrogated, God, blessed and exalted, permitted the wife of the adopted son, and the Messenger of God ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, the divorced wife of Zayd ibn Harithah, may God be pleased with him. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have concluded their need of them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]. And He, blessed and exalted, said in the verse of prohibition: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [al-Nisa: 23], excluding the wife of the adopted son, since he is not from the loins.

As for the son by nursing (ibn al-rada'ah), he is treated as a son by blood in the Shari'ah, by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in (al-Sahihayn): "Prohibit by nursing what is prohibited by lineage."

As for calling another's child "son" out of honour and affection, this is not what is forbidden in this verse, by the evidence of what Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan narrated, except al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ placed the young boys of the Banu Abd al-Muttalib upon our mounts from (Jam') and he began to slap our thighs and say: 'Little sons! Throw the pebbles until the sun rises.'"

Abu Ubaydah and others said: "Ubayni" is a diminutive of "ibni" (my son). This is clear in its indication, for this was at the Farewell Pilgrimage in the tenth year.

In Muslim, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: "O my son (ya bunayya)." Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi. End of the words of Ibn Kathir.

As for his view that the command in the verse is abrogating, there is scrutiny in it; for the abrogating ruling must cancel a prior address, whereas what has no prior address, but rather comes as a new ruling that removes the original presumption of non-liability, is not called naskh in the technical sense. So memorize this, for it is important and beneficial in several places.

When God, exalted, commanded that the lineages of adopted sons be returned to their fathers, if they are known, He pointed to their being called by brotherhood and clientage if they are not known, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿But if you do not know their fathers﴾, i.e., so that you attribute them to them, ﴿then they are your brothers﴾, i.e., they are your brothers ﴿in religion and your clients﴾, i.e., your allies in it; that is, say: "This is my brother," and "This is my client (mawla)," and "O my brother" and "O my client": ﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾, i.e., no sin, ﴿for what you have done in error﴾, i.e., in what you did of attributing some of them to other than their true father, erring through forgetfulness or inadvertence, or a slip of the tongue, because God, exalted, has lifted the burden in error and removed its sin: ﴿but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts intended﴾, i.e., in that lies the blame, because whoever intentionally does falsehood is sinful: ﴿And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e., by His pardon of the one who erred.

The commentary on His words, the Exalted:

[6] ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of blood relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you do kindness to your allies. That was written in the Book as a decree.﴾

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ means: in every matter of religion and worldly affairs. It is obligatory for them that he be dearer to them than their own selves, that his command take precedence over their own commands, that his right be more prioritized for them than their own rights, and that their compassion for him be more immediate than their compassion for themselves. They should sacrifice themselves for him, make themselves a ransom for him when a grave matter arises and a shield for him when war breaks out. They should not follow what their souls incline them to, nor what those souls turn them away from. Rather, they should follow everything that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) calls them to and everything he turns them away from, because whatever he calls to is guidance for them toward attaining salvation and succeeding in the happiness of both abodes, and whatever he turns them away from is a holding back of them, lest they fall headlong into what would drive them to wretchedness and the punishment of the Fire. This was conveyed by al-Zamakhshari.

This is as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge in what is disputed between them and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit with [full] acceptance﴾ [al-Nisa: 65]. And in the Sahih: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until I am dearer to him than his own self, his wealth, his child, and all the people." 

﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾ means: in the obligation to honour and respect them, and the prohibition of marrying them. Apart from that, they are like other non-related women. Therefore Ibn Kathir said: "However, it is not permissible to be alone with them, and the prohibition does not extend to their daughters and sisters by scholarly consensus (ijma', the agreement of scholars). Although some scholars called their daughters 'sisters of the believers,' as is the explicit statement of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, in al-Mukhtasar, this is a matter of the usage of expression, not the establishment of a ruling. Is Mu'awiya and his like to be called 'maternal uncle of the believers'? On this there are two opinions, and from al-Shafi'i it is reported that such a designation is used." And is he (ﷺ) to be called "father of the believers"? On this there are two opinions. It is authentically reported from A'isha that it is not, and this is the more correct of the two views among the Shafi'is, based on His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40]. It is also reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they recited: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them." A similar report is transmitted from Mu'awiya, Mujahid, Ikrima and al-Hasan, and they took as evidence for it the hadith which Abu Dawud related from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am to you as a father, I teach you. So when one of you comes to relieve himself, he should not face the qibla nor turn his back to it, and he should not clean himself with his right hand." This was conveyed by Ibn Kathir.

﴿And those of blood relationship﴾ means: those who are related by kinship. ﴿are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ means: in what He has prescribed, or in what He revealed to His Prophet, peace be upon him. ﴿than the [other] believers and the emigrants﴾ is an explanation of "those of blood relationship," or it is a complement to "nearer" (ula). ﴿except that you do kindness to your allies﴾ means: your fellow believers and emigrants who are not relatives, ﴿kindness﴾ meaning charity, consolation, gifts and bequests; for extending the hand in kindness is among what Allah has urged His servants to do, and it is shared with the near kin and others.

[p. 4829] Note:

In al-Iklil it is said: "He (Ibn Kathir?) used as evidence His saying, ﴿and those of blood relationship...﴾ to the end of the verse, for those who grant inheritance to dhawu al-arham (blood relatives who are not sharers or residuary heirs)." End of quote.

This is a sound inference, and the opponent has nothing to counter it. Rather, many understood by it that relatives have greater right to inheritance than the emigrants and the Helpers, and that it abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of an earlier ruling) the inheritance by alliance and brotherhood that existed between them, following what was reported from al-Zubayr and Ibn Abbas: that an emigrant would inherit from a Helper to the exclusion of his own relatives and kin, because of the brotherhood which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had established between them, until Allah revealed the verse. Thereafter we returned to our inheritance laws.

However, the derivation of this is from the general sense of the priority, not that it is restricted to the claim for which it is cited, as we have explained many times before.

﴿That was written in the Book as a decree﴾ means: in the Qur'an, or in His decree and judgment, and what He wrote and prescribed, firmly established, not subject to alteration or change.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a firm covenant.﴾

﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary﴾: That is, We took their pledges to convey the message, to call to the truth, to cooperate, support one another and be united, to establish the religion, and not to become divided over it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My command on that condition?" They said, "We affirm it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 81]. Abu al-Su'ud said: Singling them out for mention, namely His saying ﴿and from you﴾ etc., despite their being included among the prophets, serves to indicate their increased excellence and merit, and that they are among the most renowned masters of the laws and the pillars of the Ulu al-'Azm (the steadfast messengers), and the placing of our Prophet before them, peace and blessings be upon them all, is to make manifest his great rank. Al-Qasimi said in (al-Insaf): Mentioning someone first does not necessarily entail this. Do you not see his saying:

*Bahaleel* among them are Ja'far and the son of his mother, 'Ali, and among them is Ahmad, the chosen one.

Here he delayed mention of the Prophet ﷺ so as to end with him as an honour to him. Since it is established that precedence in mention does not necessarily imply superiority, what appears to be the wisdom, and God knows best, in mentioning him, peace be upon him, before Noah and those after him, is that he is the one addressed among them, and the one to whom this recited revelation was sent down, so his being mentioned first is for that reason.

Then, when he, peace be upon him, was mentioned first, the mention of the prophets, may God's blessings be upon them, followed him in the order of their times of existence. God knows best. End.

He has explicitly named the Ulu al-'Azm here, and in the verse: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein."﴾ [al-Shura: 13]. Ibn Kathir said: This is the charge which He took from them the covenant upon, ﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾, that is, a covenant of great importance. And how could it not be, when it is beset by those who scheme, oppose and contend against it, with things that would move mountains, were it not for holding fast to patience in it.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8–9] ﴿That He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when hosts came to you, so We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 9]

He placed "the truthful" in the position of their pronoun, to indicate from the outset that they are truthful in what they were asked about. Even if whoever denied them among the ignorant, the obstinate, the apostates and the transgressors denied them, what the messengers brought is the truth, and whoever opposes them is in error. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verses 10–13:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10–13] ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you were thinking about Allah with various thoughts.﴾ ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11] ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12] ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return!" And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," and they were not exposed. They intended only to flee.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]

﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you﴾: that is, from the upper part of the valley and its lower part, with the intention of forming factions so that they would be one body in order to annihilate the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾: that is, they turned away from their usual direction and level of sight, out of bewilderment and staring. ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾: that is, reached the end of the windpipe; for with fright the lungs swell and rise, and with their rising the hearts rise, and this is from the severity of distress. Or it is a metaphor for the agitation of hearts. ﴿And you were thinking about Allah with various thoughts﴾: that is, kinds of differing thoughts. ﴿There the believers were tested﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11]: that is, they were examined so that the steadfast would be distinguished from the wavering, and the believer from the hypocrite. ﴿And were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11]: that is, they were disturbed with the utmost disturbance, from the severity of fear and alarm, or from the multitude of enemies.

Benefit:

Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read "al-Zununa" (al-ẓunūnā) with an alif added after the nun, and after the lam of "al-Rasula" in His saying ﴿and we obeyed the Messenger﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66] and the lam of "al-Sabila" in His saying ﴿so they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67], both in pause and in continuation, in conformity with the orthography, because these three were written in the Mushaf in this form. Also, this alif resembles the ha' of silence (hā' al-sakt), which indicates the vowel. The hā' al-sakt is retained in pause because of the need for it, and it has been retained in continuation as well, treating continuation as pause. Likewise this alif.

Abu 'Amr and Hamza read it without the alif in both states, because it has no basis; and the saying of those who claim "the fawasil (verse-endings) were treated like the qawafi (rhyme-endings)" is not considered valid, because stopping on qawafi is generally obligatory, whereas this is not obligatory for fawasil, so they are not likened to them. The rest read it with the alif in pause and without it in continuation, treating the fawasil like the qawafi in the retention of the alif of extension (alif al-itlaq), and because it is like the hā' al-sakt, which is retained in pause and dropped in continuation. This was related by al-Samin.

Then He, exalted is He, pointed to what appeared from the hypocrites in that hardship, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12]: that is, doubt, relieving themselves with what they found of whispering in their souls, and an opportunity for their tongues to run with what their breasts conceal, owing to the weakness of their faith and the severity of their straitened condition and the enemy's encirclement of them. ﴿What Allah and His Messenger promised us﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12]: that is, of victory. ﴿Nothing but delusion﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12]: that is, falsehood. ﴿And when a faction of them said﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]: that is, of the hypocrites. ﴿O people of Yathrib﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]: and it is the land of Madinah. ﴿There is no place for you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]: with the mim pronounced with damma and with fatha, two readings; that is, there is no residence for you after today in Madinah or its environs, because of the dominance of the enemies. ﴿So return!﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]: that is, to your dwellings in Madinah, fleeing; or, return from Islam as disbelievers so that you may remain.

Benefit:

(Yathrib) is among the names of Madinah, as in the Sahih: "I was shown in a dream the land of your migration, a land between two lava fields. My thought went that it was Hajar, but it was Yathrib." In another wording: "al-Madinah."

Ibn Kathir said: As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever names Madinah 'Yathrib' should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted; it is only Taba, it is Taba." Imam Ahmad alone narrated it, and its chain contains weakness. End.

﴿And a faction of them asked permission of the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]: that is, to return. ﴿Saying, "Indeed our houses are exposed"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]: that is, not fortified, and they fear for them. ﴿And they were not exposed; they intended only to flee﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13].

[14–16] "And if it had been entered upon them from all its sides, and they had been asked to commit fitnah (apostasy), they would have given it, and they would not have delayed in it except briefly." (p-4834) "And they had already pledged to Allah before, that they would not turn their backs, and the pledge of Allah will be questioned." [Al-Ahzab: 15] "Say: Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little." [Al-Ahzab: 16]

"And if it had been entered" – i.e., Yathrib – "upon them from its sides" – i.e., if the enemy had entered upon them from all its surrounding areas and began plundering and looting. "Then they were asked for fitnah" – i.e., the return to disbelief – "they would have given it" – i.e., they would have done it – "and they would not have delayed in it except briefly" – i.e., they would not have hesitated in giving it except for the time it takes for the question and answer. That is, they do not guard faith or hold fast to it, even with the slightest fear and alarm. This is the utmost blame of them. Then Allah, exalted is He, reminded them of what they had pledged to Him before, by His words: "And they had already pledged to Allah before" [Al-Ahzab: 15] – i.e., before this fear – "that they would not turn their backs, and the pledge of Allah will be questioned" [Al-Ahzab: 15] – i.e., concerning fulfilling it. "Say: Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing" [Al-Ahzab: 16] – i.e., because it does not postpone their appointed terms, nor prolong their lives. Rather, it may perhaps be a cause for hastening their being seized unawares as retribution from Him. For this reason He said: "And then" [Al-Ahzab: 16] – i.e., if you flee – "you will not be given enjoyment except for a little" [Al-Ahzab: 16] – i.e., in this world after your flight; or because by that they forfeit their share of the Hereafter, so however much they are given enjoyment in this world, it is little in comparison with the bliss of the Hereafter for the patient.

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[17–19] ﴿Say: "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm, or intends for you mercy?" They will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any ally or any helper.﴾ ﴿Allah already knows those among you who discourage others, and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and they do not approach battle except a little.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18] (p-4835) ﴿Stingy towards you. So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who is overcome by death. But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues, stingy regarding goodness. Those have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is ever easy for Allah.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19]

﴿Say: "Who is it that can protect you"﴾, i.e., who can grant you protection (ijarah): ﴿from Allah if He intends for you harm﴾, i.e., destruction or defeat, ﴿or intends for you mercy﴾. ﴿They will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any ally or any helper﴾, i.e., any protector (mujir) or any aid who will repel harm from them.

﴿Allah already knows those among you who discourage others﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], i.e., those who dissuade (mutha'bitin) others from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they are the hypocrites (munafiqun). Al-Shihab said: "The word qad (قد) is for emphasis (tahqiq), or for limitation (taqlil) with regard to its object, and in relation to what is not known to Him." End of quote.

﴿And those who say to their brothers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], i.e., from among the residents of Madinah: ﴿"Come to us"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], i.e., turn towards what we are engaged in of misguidance and [the fruits of] ... ; ﴿and they do not approach battle﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], i.e., fighting, ﴿except a little﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], i.e., they come only a little, because they discourage [others] as much as they are able.

﴿Stingy towards you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19], i.e., withholding help, expenditure and affection from you, or, outwardly, showing you little sincere concern, if no fear arises. ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19], i.e., in their sockets; ﴿like one who is overcome by death﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19], i.e., like the gaze or the rolling of one whose eyes are fixed in a death-like stupor.

﴿But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19], i.e., they go to excess against you with speech, through reproach and defamation, so they scorch you and harm you. The root of (salq) is extending and stretching a limb for the purpose of subduing, whether it is a hand or a tongue. It is permissible to liken the tongue to a sword by way of metaphor (isti'arah makniyyah), attributing to it the act of striking (salq), which is a striking by imagination (takhyil).

﴿Stingy regarding goodness﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19], i.e., regarding its performance. ﴿Those have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19].

(p-4836)On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20–21] ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn; and if the confederates should come, they would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins, asking about your news. And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.﴾ ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone who hopes for Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21]

﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾ meaning: they have not been defeated by what was sent upon them of the wind and the troops, and they think that the confederates will return to them because of their weakness and disorder. ﴿And if the confederates should come﴾ meaning: once again. ﴿They would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾ meaning: they would not go out to fight them, nor would they remain in Madinah; rather they would wish that they were out in the open country among the Bedouins, even though the shame of their cowardice would befall them. ﴿Asking﴾ meaning: the arrivals ﴿about your news﴾ meaning: about what happened to you. Then Allah, exalted is He, indicated that their departure from Madinah, should the confederates come, would not harm them, by His saying: ﴿And if they were among you﴾ meaning: in the occurrence of a second event. ﴿They would not fight except a little﴾ meaning: for show and out of fear of being reproached.

﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21] meaning: in his character and actions there is an excellent example, for in them is his steadfastness in hardships, which is required, and his patience over adversity and affliction, while he is distressed and besieged, and his soul remains calm amid changing circumstances; he does not weaken in a severe trial nor submit to a great or grave matter. He met in Makkah from Quraysh what would turn the forelocks gray and break the strongholds, and despite his weakness he endured with the patience of one who prevails and stood firm with the steadfastness of one who dominates. Whoever is patient through these hardships in calling to Allah, exalted is He, while he is of exalted rank, others are more worthy of it, if they are among those who follow him in goodness: ﴿for anyone who hopes for Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21] meaning: the good pleasure of Allah, His mercy, the reward of the Last Day, and its salvation; for he prefers these two over the worldly life, so he does not act cowardly, since cowardice is not valid for one who correctly follows the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), given its extreme ugliness. ﴿And remembers Allah often﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21] meaning: he combines hope with frequent remembrance of Allah, exalted is He; that is, he remembers His command, His prohibition, His promise and His threat, so he perceives the places of happiness and the precipices of wretchedness, and he knows that steadfastness in killing the enemy purifies the earth from corruption and adorns it with truth, righteousness and rectitude, the reward of which is the happiness of both abodes and the success of the two good outcomes.

Then Allah, exalted is He, clarified what the sincere believers did in that severe hardship, after clarifying what others did, by His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verses 22–23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22–23] ﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth." And it increased them only in faith and submission.﴾ ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah. Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow [by death], and among them is one who awaits. And they did not alter [their pledge] at all.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23].

﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us"﴾: that is, because He, exalted is He, promised them that they would be shaken until they called upon Him for help and sought His support, in His saying: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise without there having come to you the like of those who passed away before you?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. Likewise the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, informed them of the trial and testing which would be followed by victory and security. ﴿"And Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth"﴾: that is, the truthfulness of the two became manifest in what they had promised us. ﴿"And it increased them"﴾: that is, this calamity and trial, ﴿"only in faith"﴾: that is, in Allah and His Messenger and their promises, ﴿"and submission"﴾: that is, to the command of Allah and His decrees, at the time of the shaking of the hypocrites and their spreading of rumours.

﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23]: in patience and steadfastness, and in carrying out what was prescribed for them of fighting, to raise high the word of truth, and in acting upon righteous deeds and avoiding evil deeds. ﴿Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23]: that is, he discharged what he had committed himself to and fulfilled it, so he fought alongside the Messenger ﷺ sincerely until he was killed as a martyr.

(p-4838) Al-Shihab said: The original meaning of (al-nahb) is a vow, and its fulfilment (qada') is carrying it out. Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, had vowed that if they witnessed a battle with him ﷺ, they would fight until they were martyred. The expression (qada' al-nahb) has been used figuratively for death, because death is unavoidable, and so it is likened to a vow which must be fulfilled. Therefore it may be literal here, or a figurative usage arising from the principle of association (mushakalah). End of quotation.

﴿And among them is one who awaits﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23]: that is, [awaiting] what Allah promised of His help and martyrdom, following the course which his companions had followed. ﴿"And they did not alter [their pledge] at all"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23]: that is, they did not change anything of the covenant, nor break it as the hypocrites broke it by turning away, in His saying: ﴿And they had already pledged to Allah before that they would not turn their backs﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15]. In it there is an allusive implicit metaphor (kinayah ta'ridiyyah), understood from the specifying of them with it, and the explicit mention of the verbal noun (tabdil) serves to convey generality.

[24–25] ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿And Allah turned back those who disbelieved, in their rage, not having obtained any good. And Allah spared the believers from fighting. And Allah is ever Strong and Mighty.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25].

﴿That Allah may reward the truthful﴾, i.e., in their covenants, ﴿for their truthfulness﴾, ﴿and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿And Allah turned back those who disbelieved, in their rage﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25], i.e., with their complete fury, by what He sent of the wind and the armies, by His bounty and mercy. ﴿Not having obtained any good﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25], i.e., victory, not spoils. ﴿And Allah spared the believers from fighting﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25], i.e., He did not make them need to confront them in battle to drive them out of Madinah. Rather, He alone took charge of sufficing them in that. For this reason, "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: 'There is no god but Allah alone. He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, honored His army, and defeated the confederates alone. (Mention of the detailed account of the news of the Confederates, known as the Battle of the Trench [Ghazwat al-Khandaq])

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Zad al-Ma'ad*: The Battle of the Trench occurred in the fifth year after the Hijrah, in Shawwal, according to the more correct of the two opinions, since there is no dispute that Uhud occurred in Shawwal of the third year. He argued against it with the hadith of Ibn Umar in the *Two Sahihs*: "He was presented to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uhud when he was fourteen years old, and he did not allow him. Then he was presented to him on the day of the Trench when he was fifteen years old, and he permitted him." He said: "It is also established that there was only one year between them."

This was answered in two ways. The first: Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet ﷺ sent him back when he considered him too young for fighting, and permitted him when he reached the age at which he saw him as capable. There is nothing in this that negates that the interval between them was a year or thereabouts.

The second: Perhaps the day of Uhud was at the beginning of his fourteenth year, and the day of the Trench at the end of his fifteenth year.

Then Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The cause of the Battle of the Trench was that "the Jews, when they saw the victory of the polytheists over the Muslims on the day of Uhud, and learned of Abu Sufyan's appointment to fight the Muslims, and he went out for that, then returned the following year, their leaders went out, such as Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Sallam ibn Mishkam, Kinana ibn al-Rabi' and others, to Quraysh in Makkah, inciting them to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and allying with them against him, and promised them from themselves victory for them. Quraysh responded to them. Then they went out to Ghatafan and called them, and they responded to them. Then they circled among the tribes of the Arabs calling them to that, and whoever responded, responded."

So Quraysh went out, their commander being Abu Sufyan, with four thousand men. Banu Sulaym met them at Marr al-Zahran. Banu Asad, Fazara, Ashja' and Banu Murra went out, and Ghatafan came, their commander being Uyayna ibn al-Hisn. There had reached the Trench from the disbelievers ten thousand.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of their march towards him, he consulted the Companions. Salman al-Farisi advised him to dig a trench that would prevent the enemy from reaching Madinah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered it, and the Muslims hastened to it. He himself worked on it, and they hastened. The disbelievers attacked them. In its digging were signs of his prophethood and marks of his mission, as the report of them has been widely transmitted. The digging of the Trench was in front of Sal'. Sal' is a mountain behind the backs of the Muslims, and the Trench was between them and the disbelievers. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out with three thousand Muslims, and he took refuge with the mountain behind him and with the Trench in front of them.

Ibn Ishaq said he went out with seven hundred. (This is an error from his going out on the day of Uhud.)

The Prophet ﷺ ordered the women and children to be placed in the fortresses (*atam*) of Madinah, and he appointed Ibn Umm Maktum as his deputy over them. Huyayy ibn Akhtab set out to Banu Qurayza and approached their fortress. Ka'b ibn Asad refused to open it for him, but he continued speaking to him until he opened it. When he entered upon him, he said: "I have brought you the honor of the age. I have brought you Quraysh, Ghatafan and Asad with their leaders to fight Muhammad." He said: Ka'b said: "You have come to me, by Allah, with the humiliation of the age and with a cloud that has poured out its water, and it is only thunder and lightning." He continued with him until he broke the covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and entered into fighting him along with the polytheists, and the polytheists rejoiced at that. Ka'b stipulated with Huyayy that if they did not triumph over Muhammad, he would come and enter with him into his fortress, and what befell him would befall him. Huyayy agreed to that and fulfilled it for him.

The news of Banu Qurayza and their breaking of the covenant reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he sent to them al-Sa'dayn, Khawwat ibn Jubayr and Abdullah ibn Rawaha, to find out whether they were upon their covenant or had broken it. When they approached them, they found them in the worst state, and they openly reviled them and bore enmity, and they insulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they turned away from them, and they spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in an allusive manner informing him that they had broken the covenant and betrayed. This was grievous to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: "Allahu Akbar! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!"

[p. 4841] The trial intensified and hypocrisy became open. Some of Banu Haritha asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to go to Madinah, saying: "Our houses are exposed," though they were not exposed; they only intended to flee. Banu Salama intended to lose heart, then Allah made both groups firm.

The polytheists remained besieging the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a month, and there was no fighting between them, because of the Trench that Allah had placed between them and the Muslims, except that some horsemen of Quraysh, among them Amr ibn Abd Wudd and a group with him, approached the Trench. When they stopped at it, they said: "This is a stratagem the Arabs did not know." Then they sought a narrow place in the Trench and forced their way across it, and their horses roamed with them in the salt flat between the Trench and Sal'. They called for single combat, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, was appointed against Amr. He fought him, and Allah killed him at his hands. He was one of the bravest and champions of the polytheists, and the rest fled back to their companions. The slogan of the Muslims that day was: "Ha Mim, they will not be helped."

When this situation was prolonged for the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to make a settlement with Uyayna ibn Hisn and al-Harith ibn Awf, the two chiefs of Ghatafan, by giving them a third of Madinah's produce, and that they would withdraw with their people. Negotiations on that took place, and he consulted the two Sa'ds about it. They said: "O Messenger of Allah! If Allah has commanded you with this, then we hear and obey. And if it is something you do for us, we have no need for it. We were, we and these people, upon polytheism and worshipping idols, and they did not expect to eat any of its fruit except as hospitality or by purchase. So when Allah honored us with Islam and guided us to it and strengthened us by you, shall we give them our wealth? By Allah! We will give them nothing but the sword." He approved their opinion and said: "This was only something I was doing for you, since I saw the Arabs had shot at you from one bow."

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to Him be praise, brought about a matter from Himself, by which He sowed discord among the enemy, defeated their hosts and blunted their edge. Among what He arranged in this was that a man from Ghatafan called Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I have embraced Islam, so command me as you wish." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You are only one man, so cause discord among them as much as you can, for war is deception." He went immediately to Banu Qurayza, and he had been their companion in the pre-Islamic period. He entered upon them while they did not know of his Islam, and said: "O Banu Qurayza! You have fought Muhammad, and if Quraysh find an opportunity they will seize it, otherwise they will retreat to their lands, leaving you and Muhammad, and he will take revenge on you." They said: "What is to be done, O Nu'aym?" He said: "Do not fight with them until they give you hostages." They said: "You have given sound counsel." Then he went on his way to Quraysh and said to them: "You know my affection for you and my counsel to you." They said: "Yes." He said: "The Jews have regretted what they did in breaking the covenant with Muhammad and his Companions, and they have sent to him that they will take hostages from you to hand over to him, then they will ally with him against you. So if they ask you for hostages, do not give them." Then he went to Ghatafan and said to them the same. When it was the night of Saturday in Shawwal, they sent to the Jews: "We are not in a place to stay, and the horses and camels have perished. So rise with us until we attack Muhammad." The Jews sent to them: "Today is Saturday, and you know what befell those before us when they transgressed on it. Moreover, we will not fight with you until you send us hostages." When their messengers came to them with that, Quraysh said: "Nu'aym has told you the truth, by Allah!" They sent to the Jews: "By Allah, we will not send anyone to you. So come out with us until we attack Muhammad." Qurayza said: "Nu'aym has told you the truth, by Allah!" Thus the two parties let each other down. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent upon the polytheists an army of wind on cold, stormy nights, of intense cold. It overturned their tents and left them no cooking pot without spilling it, no tent peg without uprooting it, and no stability remained for them, while the army of Allah from the angels shook them and cast terror and fear into their hearts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Huthayfa ibn al-Yaman to bring him news of them. He found them in this state, and they were ready to depart. He returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of the departure of the people. In the morning, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had with him that Allah had turned back His enemy in their rage, not having obtained any good, and Allah had spared them from fighting. He fulfilled His promise, honored His army, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone.

Then when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to Madinah, aided and victorious, with the Muslims with him, and they laid down their arms, and it was the time of noon prayer, Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands you to march against Banu Qurayza, a tribe of the Jews of Khaybar. I am going to them to shake them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a caller, and he called among [p. 4843] the people: "Whoever is hearing and obedient, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayza." He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, ahead with his banner to Banu Qurayza, and the people hastened to it. Ali marched until, when he approached the fortresses, he heard from them an ugly saying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he returned until he met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the road. He said: "O Messenger of Allah! Let it not concern you that you do not approach these wicked people." He said: "Why? I think you heard from them some harm to me." He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If they had seen me, they would not have said anything of that." The people caught up with him, and he besieged them for twenty-five nights until the siege exhausted them, and Allah cast terror into their hearts. Then they came down under the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Aws then rose up and said: "O Messenger of Allah! May Allah bless you and grant you peace. They were our clients (*mawali*) rather than the Khazraj, and you have done with the clients of our brothers yesterday what you know."

[p. 4844]

Before the Banu Qurayza, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had besieged the Banu Qaynuqa', a tribe of Jews who lived in Medina and were allies of the Khazraj. They surrendered to his judgment, and 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul interceded for them, so he granted them to him.

When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge concerning them?" They said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then the matter rests with Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had placed Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in the tent of a woman of Aslam called Rufayda, in his mosque. She would treat the wounded and devoted herself to caring for whichever Muslim was afflicted. When an arrow struck Sa'd at the Trench, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to his people: "Place him in the tent of Rufayda, so that I may visit him from nearby." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him to judge concerning the Banu Qurayza, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey.

He was a large and handsome man. They then went with him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Stand up for your master (sayyid)." So they stood up for him and helped him down.

Ibn Kathir said: [This was] out of honour, respect and reverence for him, in the place of his authority, so that his judgment concerning them would be more binding.

When he sat down, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "These people have surrendered to your judgment, so judge concerning them as you wish." The Aws began to approach him, urging that he show them kindness, and saying: "O Abu 'Amr! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has entrusted you with the affair of your clients, so that you may judge concerning them."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Upon you is the covenant and pledge of Allah, that the judgment concerning them is what I decide." They said: "Yes." He said: "And upon the one who is here" (in the direction where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, and he turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) out of reverence for him) — "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Yes.'" Sa'd said: "I judge concerning them that the men be put to death, the wealth be divided, and the children (dhurriyya) and women be taken captive."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Sa'd: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." In another narration: "You have judged by the judgment of the King," meaning: because this is the recompense of the treacherous betrayer.

Sa'd had been struck on the day of the Trench: a man of Quraysh called Ibn al-'Araqa had shot him in the akhal (a vein of the arm). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cauterized his akhal. Sa'd said: "O Allah! If You have left any of the war with Quraysh, then preserve me for it, for there is no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who harmed Your Messenger, denied him and expelled him. O Allah! And if You have ended the war between us and them, then grant me martyrdom, and do not cause me to die until my eye is comforted concerning the Banu Qurayza." So Allah answered his supplication, and decreed that they would come down to his judgment of their own accord, seeking it of their own will.

Then, when they were brought down from their fortresses, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confined them in a house in Medina. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market of Medina and dug trenches there. Then he sent for them and beheaded them in those trenches, bringing them out to him in groups. Among them was the enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six hundred or seven hundred. Those among them who had not yet grown up were taken captive along with the women and their wealth.

This is what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned concerning the affair of the Banu Qurayza, following the affair of the Trench, with His saying, glorified is He:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a caller, and he called among [p. 4843] the people: "Whoever is hearing and obedient, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayza." He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, ahead with his banner to Banu Qurayza, and the people hastened to it. Ali marched until, when he approached the fortresses, he heard from them an ugly saying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he returned until he met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the road. He said: "O Messenger of Allah! Let it not concern you that you do not approach these wicked people." He said: "Why? I think you heard from them some harm to me." He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If they had seen me, they would not have said anything of that." The people caught up with him, and he besieged them for twenty-five nights until the siege exhausted them, and Allah cast terror into their hearts. Then they came down under the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Aws then rose up and said: "O Messenger of Allah! May Allah bless you and grant you peace. They were our clients (*mawali*) rather than the Khazraj, and you have done with the clients of our brothers yesterday what you know."

[p. 4844]

Before the Banu Qurayza, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had besieged the Banu Qaynuqa', a tribe of Jews who lived in Medina and were allies of the Khazraj. They surrendered to his judgment, and 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul interceded for them, so he granted them to him.

When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge concerning them?" They said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then the matter rests with Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had placed Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in the tent of a woman of Aslam called Rufayda, in his mosque. She would treat the wounded and devoted herself to caring for whichever Muslim was afflicted. When an arrow struck Sa'd at the Trench, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to his people: "Place him in the tent of Rufayda, so that I may visit him from nearby." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him to judge concerning the Banu Qurayza, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey.

He was a large and handsome man. They then went with him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Stand up for your master (sayyid)." So they stood up for him and helped him down.

Ibn Kathir said: [This was] out of honour, respect and reverence for him, in the place of his authority, so that his judgment concerning them would be more binding.

When he sat down, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "These people have surrendered to your judgment, so judge concerning them as you wish." The Aws began to approach him, urging that he show them kindness, and saying: "O Abu 'Amr! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has entrusted you with the affair of your clients, so that you may judge concerning them."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Upon you is the covenant and pledge of Allah, that the judgment concerning them is what I decide." They said: "Yes." He said: "And upon the one who is here" (in the direction where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, and he turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) out of reverence for him) — "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Yes.'" Sa'd said: "I judge concerning them that the men be put to death, the wealth be divided, and the children (dhurriyya) and women be taken captive."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Sa'd: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." In another narration: "You have judged by the judgment of the King," meaning: because this is the recompense of the treacherous betrayer.

Sa'd had been struck on the day of the Trench: a man of Quraysh called Ibn al-'Araqa had shot him in the akhal (a vein of the arm). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cauterized his akhal. Sa'd said: "O Allah! If You have left any of the war with Quraysh, then preserve me for it, for there is no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who harmed Your Messenger, denied him and expelled him. O Allah! And if You have ended the war between us and them, then grant me martyrdom, and do not cause me to die until my eye is comforted concerning the Banu Qurayza." So Allah answered his supplication, and decreed that they would come down to his judgment of their own accord, seeking it of their own will.

Then, when they were brought down from their fortresses, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confined them in a house in Medina. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market of Medina and dug trenches there. Then he sent for them and beheaded them in those trenches, bringing them out to him in groups. Among them was the enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six hundred or seven hundred. Those among them who had not yet grown up were taken captive along with the women and their wealth.

This is what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned concerning the affair of the Banu Qurayza, following the affair of the Trench, with His saying, glorified is He:

(p-٤٨٤5) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26–28] ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses and cast fear into their hearts. A part you killed, and you took captive a part.﴾ ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And ever is Allah over all things competent.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 27] ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: "If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28]

﴿And He brought down those who supported them﴾ means: who aided the confederates and assisted them in fighting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ﴿From the People of the Scripture﴾ refers to the Banu Qurayzah, a group of the Jews whose forefathers had settled in the Hijaz after fleeing persecution and had scattered in every direction across the lands. ﴿From their fortresses﴾ means from their strongholds and their towers in which they were. ﴿And He cast fear into their hearts﴾ means terror, as a fitting recompense.

Ibn Kathir said: Because they had colluded with the polytheists against the Prophet ﷺ — "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" — and had frightened the Muslims and sought to kill them in order to gain power in this world, the situation was reversed upon them, and the fighting turned back against them, when the polytheists withdrew and departed with the deal of one who has been cheated. Just as they sought honor, they were humiliated; and as they intended to uproot the Muslims, they were uprooted. Therefore He, exalted, said: ﴿A part you killed, and you took captive a part﴾, meaning the killing of the fighting men and the taking captive of the children and women.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Atiyyah al-Qurazi who said: "I was presented to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Qurayzah, and they doubted about me. So the Prophet ﷺ ordered that they examine me: has he grown hair yet? They examined me and did not find that I had grown hair, so he released me and counted me among the captives."

Likewise, all the compilers of the Sunan narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes﴾ [al-Ahzab: 27], meaning their fortresses; ﴿and their wealth﴾ [al-Ahzab: 27], meaning their money, their goods and their livestock; ﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾ [al-Ahzab: 27], meaning a land you had not yet taken possession of, namely Khaybar, and it was said Makkah. Malik narrated it from Zayd ibn Aslam. And it was said: Persia and Rome. Ibn Jarir said: it is permissible that all of these are intended. Al-Zamakhshari said: Among the strange interpretations is that it means their women.

With the completion of this campaign, Allah relieved the Muslims of the evil of the neighbourhood of the Jews, who were accustomed to treachery and betrayal, and there remained only a remnant of their elders at Khaybar together with its people, and they were the cause of inciting the confederates. Some of them said: O God! How evil is the outcome of rashness! A nation may be at ease and calm of heart, until a group of its leaders commits an act of treachery, supposing success will follow it, and it brings upon them evils and scatters them from their homes.

This is what happened to the Jews in the Hijaz. There were covenants between them and the Muslims by which each felt safe from the other, but the Jews did not fulfil those covenants, out of envy and transgression. So what befell them befell them, as the way of Allah with the corrupters, for Allah does not set right the works of the corrupt: ﴿And ever is Allah over all things competent﴾ [al-Ahzab: 27], meaning: you have witnessed some of His decrees, so take warning from others.

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: "If you should desire the worldly life﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28], meaning its ease and luxury; ﴿and its adornment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28], meaning its embellishments; ﴿then come, I will provide for you and release you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28], meaning I will give you the mut'ah (provision) and divorce you. Mut'ah is what is given to a divorced woman according to one's means and straitness, of clothing or dirhams or furnishings, as a voluntary act, not an obligation. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a fair release﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28], meaning a divorce without harm or innovation.

It has been related that they asked the Prophet ﷺ for garments of adornment and an increase in maintenance from what he did not have. So the verse was revealed. When it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ began with ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, as she was the dearest of them to him; he gave her the choice and recited the Qur'an to her, and she chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. Then all of them chose as she had chosen. It was said: At that time he had nine wives under him, five from Quraysh: ʿĀ'ishah, Ḥafṣah, Umm Ḥabībah, Sawdah, and Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with them; then Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy al-Naḍriyyah, Maymunah bint al-Ḥārith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jaḥsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyyah bint al-Ḥārith al-Muṣṭaliqiyyah, may Allah be pleased with them.

Al-Razi said: The connection is that noble character is confined to two things: reverence for the command of Allah, and compassion toward the creation of Allah. To this the Prophet, peace be upon him, alluded with his saying: "Prayer, and what your right hands possess." Then, when Allah, exalted, guided His Prophet to what relates to the aspect of reverence for Allah, by saying: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 1], He mentioned what relates to the aspect of compassion, and began with the wives, for they are the people most deserving of compassion; and for this reason he placed them first in maintenance. End.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29–30] ﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Home, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a manifest immorality, her punishment will be doubled twofold. And that is ever easy for Allah.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30].

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Home⦈ means: you desire His Messenger. Abu al-Su'ud said: The mention of Allah, mighty and majestic, is to signal the exalted station of his (peace be upon him) with Him, exalted is He: ﴿then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward⦈, meaning, its worth cannot be measured. When the Prophet (ﷺ) gave them the choice, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah disciplined them and warned them, so that they would avoid what displeases the Prophet (ﷺ) and what is ugly for them of immorality. He threatened them with doubling of the punishment through His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a manifest immorality⦈ [al-Ahzab: 30], meaning: it is manifest between the Shari'ah and reason as being ugly, if it is read with a fatha, i.e., *mubayyinatin* (manifest), or *mubayyinatin* meaning making its ugliness evident in itself without reflection, if it is read with a kasra. ﴿Her punishment will be doubled twofold⦈ [al-Ahzab: 30], meaning: twice the punishment of others. The judge (al-Qadi) said: Because the sin from them is more ugly, for the increase in its ugliness follows the increase in the sinner's merit and in the blessing bestowed upon them. For this reason the prescribed punishment for a free person was made twice that of a slave, and the Prophets were rebuked for things for which others are not rebuked. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah⦈ [al-Ahzab: 30], because of the all-encompassing scope of His power.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[31–33] ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a generous provision.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire, but speak in a fair manner.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32] ﴿And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33]

﴿And whoever of you devotes herself﴾, i.e., continues in obedience. ﴿To God and His Messenger﴾, i.e., in performing the obligations and abstaining from what is forbidden and disliked. ﴿And does righteous deeds﴾, ﴿We will give her her reward twice over﴾, i.e., once for obedience and piety, and once for seeking the pleasure of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) through good character, pleasant companionship, and contentment. ﴿And We have prepared for her﴾, i.e., in addition to her doubled reward, in Paradise, or in it and in this world, ﴿a generous provision﴾, i.e., a good and pleasing one.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, do not be soft in speech﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., when addressing people. That is: do not answer with a soft, languid tone like the speech of women who arouse suspicion and of immoral women. ﴿Lest one in whose heart is a disease﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., doubt and debauchery, ﴿should feel desire﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32]. ﴿But speak in a fair manner﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., far from arousing the desire of one who harbors doubt, speak with seriousness and firmness, without softness; or, speak good words while being rough.

﴿And remain in your houses﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., stay and do not go out from them. It is from (waqara, yaqiru, waqaran), meaning "he became settled," or from (qarra, yaqirru, from the pattern of daraba), where the first of the two identical r's in (iqrarna, "remain") was dropped, and its vowel was transferred to the qaf, so the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with. This is supported by the reading of Nafi' and Asim with a fath (fatha), from (qarirtu, aqarru), from the pattern of ʿalima, which is a rare dialect. ﴿And do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., the display of women in the days of the first jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance, the age of disbelief). For there was no religion restraining them nor good manners holding them back. Tabarruj (display) has been explained as swaying and affected gait in walking, as showing adornment and what arouses a man's desire, as wearing thin clothing that does not conceal the body, and as displaying the beauty of the neck, necklaces, and earrings. All of this falls within the prohibition, because of the harm it contains and because it exposes one to a grave sin.

**Benefit:**
It has been said: "al-Ula" (the first) means "the former" in an unrestricted sense, without being limited to a particular time. Thus it is used as evidence for those who say that the first does not necessarily imply a second. In al-Iklil it is said: "This is the soundest view among scholars. So if someone says, 'The first child you bear, you are divorced,' she does not need to bear a second child." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "al-Ula is the ancient (jahiliyyah) that is called the jahiliyyah of the ignorant, from the time in which Abraham was born, or before it, until the time of Jesus. The jahiliyyah is what lies between Jesus and Muhammad, may the blessings of God be upon them both. It is also possible that the first jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of disbelief before Islam, and the other jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of sin and immorality within Islam. This is supported by what is narrated: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Abu Dhar, when he reproached a man for his mother, who was non-Arab: 'You are a man in whom there is jahiliyyah.'"

The meaning is a prohibition against them introducing a jahiliyyah into Islam, resembling the jahiliyyah of disbelief that came before it. ﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., by complying with their command and prohibition. Then He indicated that opposing them is impurity, which does not befit the virtue of the People of the House, in His words: ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., what He commanded you, forbade you, and admonished you about, is only out of fear of committing sins and eagerness to guard yourselves from them through piety. Thus the clause is causal, explaining His command and prohibition to them, as a fresh statement (isti'naf, a new clause).

(p. 4850) Al-Zamakhshari said: "He used 'impurity' (rijs) as a metaphor for sins, and 'purity' (tuhr) for piety, because the honor of one who commits abominations becomes soiled and defiled by them, just as his body becomes soiled by filth. As for virtuous deeds, the honor with them is pure and protected, like a clean garment. In this metaphor there is something that repels people of understanding from what God dislikes for His servants and forbade them, and encourages them toward what He is pleased with for them and commanded them to do."

﴿The People of the House﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] is in the accusative, either as a vocative or as a praise. What is meant by them is those whom the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) encompasses.

Ibn Kathir said: "This is an explicit text that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are included among the People of the House here, because they were the cause of the revelation of this verse, and the cause of revelation is undoubtedly included in it, either alone according to one opinion, or together with others according to the sound view. As for the statement of Ikrimah, that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically, and whoever wishes, I will challenge him on this, if what is meant is that they were the cause of the revelation and not others, then it is correct. But if what is meant is that they alone are intended to the exclusion of others, then there is room for examination, for there are hadiths indicating that what is meant is more general than that, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, then covered them with a cloak he had, and then said: 'These are my People of the House, so remove the impurity from them.'"

Ibn Kathir cited the chains of this hadith and those who transmitted it, but the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not authenticate it, and therefore did not include it. As for what Muslim narrated from Husayn ibn Sabrah, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Now then, O people! I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will answer. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of God, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of God and hold fast to it." He urged them to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and encouraged them toward it. Then he said: "And my People of the House. I remind you of God regarding my People of the House," and he said it three times. Husayn said to him: "And who are the People of his House, O Zayd? Are not his wives of his House?" He said: "His wives are of his House, but his People of the House are those for whom charity has been forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "The family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them" (p. 4851). Then what Zayd meant is his family who forbade charity; or it is that the People of the House is not meant as the wives alone, but they together with his family. Ibn Kathir said: "This is the more probable view, combining the Qur'an and the preceding hadiths, if they are sound, for there is some scrutiny regarding some of their chains."

Abu al-Su'ud said: "This, as you see, is a clear verse and a luminous proof that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are of his People of the House, decisively invalidating the view of the Shi'a in restricting the status of the People of the House to Fatimah, 'Ali, and their two sons, may God be pleased with them. As for what they cling to of the hadith of the cloak, and the Prophet's recitation of the verse after it, it indicates only that they are of the People of the House, not that others are not. And even if its indication of that were granted, it would not be considered, because it stands against an explicit text."

It remains that the Shi'a also cited the verse as evidence for the infallibility ('ismah) of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, and his imamate to the exclusion of others. Ibn al-Mutahhar al-Hilli, one of them, said: "In this verse is evidence of infallibility, with the emphasis of the word 'innama' (indeed, only), the inclusion of the lam in the predicate, and the specificity in the address with His words: ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], and others are not infallible, etc." Ibn Taymiyyah, may God have mercy on him, answered in (Minhaj al-Sunnah) with the words: "There is no evidence in this for their infallibility or their imamate. The verification of this is in two respects.

The first: His words ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] are like His words: ﴿God does not intend to place upon you any difficulty﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 6], and like His words: ﴿God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 185], and like His words: ﴿God intends to make clear to you and to guide you to the traditions of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness; and God is Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa': 26], ﴿And God intends to accept your repentance, while those who follow desires intend that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ [An-Nisa': 27]. For God's intention in these verses includes His love for that intended matter and His pleasure with it, and that He legislated it for the believers and commanded them to do it. It does not mean that He created this intended matter, nor that He decreed and determined it, nor that it will necessarily occur. The evidence for this is that after the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O God, these are my People of the House, so remove the impurity from them and purify them with complete purification.'
