He asked God on their behalf to remove the impurity and to purify them. Had the verse contained God's report that He had already removed the impurity from them and purified them, there would have been no need for request and supplication.

This is clearer according to the view of the Qadariyyah (the group who deny divine predestination in human acts). For their intention of God does not entail the existence of what is intended; rather He may intend what does not occur and what occurs He does not intend. So His being intending that does not indicate its occurrence.

This Rafidi (a term for the Shi'a) and his like are Qadariyyah, so how can they argue from His words ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] for the occurrence of what is intended? For according to them God intended the faith of everyone on the earth, yet His intention did not come to pass. As for the view of the affirmers (of divine decree), the verification in this matter is that the intention in the Book of God is of two kinds: a legislative, religious intention, which entails His love and His pleasure; and a universal, decreed intention, which entails His creation and His decree. The first is like these verses, and the second is like His words: ﴿Whomever God intends to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; and whomever He intends to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ [Al-An'am: 125], and the words of Noah: ﴿My advice will not benefit you if I wished to advise you, if God intends to lead you astray﴾ [Hud: 34].

Many of the affirmers and the Qadariyyah make intention one kind, just as they make intention and love one thing. Then the Qadariyyah negate His intention for what the legislation shows to be intended in the verses; for according to them, whatever is said to be intended does not necessarily exist. God has informed us that He intends to turn in forgiveness to the believers and to purify them, and among them are those who repented and those who did not repent, and among them are those who became pure and those who did not become pure. And if the verse indicates the occurrence of what He intended of purification and removal of impurity, it does not follow from the verse alone that what he claims is established."

Among the things that clarify this is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are explicitly mentioned in the verse, and the discussion concerns the command to purification through making it obligatory, the promise of reward for doing it, and the punishment for neglecting it. God the Exalted says: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold, and that is easy for God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30], up to His words: ﴿And obey God and His Messenger. God only intends to remove from you the uncleanness, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. The address is entirely to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and with them are the commands, prohibitions, promises and threats. However, when the benefit of this became clear, namely that it encompasses them and extends to others among the People of the House, the purification came with this address and other things, not exclusive to his wives. Rather, it encompasses all the People of the House, and ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the most particularly included in it over others. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ singled them out for supplication on their behalf. This is like His saying: ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 108], which was revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba, yet the ruling encompasses it and what is more worthy of it, namely the Mosque of Medina. This clarifies what is established in the Sahih from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about the mosque founded upon piety, and he said: "It is this mosque of mine." It is also established from him in the Sahih that he used to go to Quba every Saturday, on foot and riding, and he would stand in his mosque on Friday and come to Quba on Saturday, and both are founded upon piety. Likewise his wives, ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, are more particularly included in this than his wives; for this reason he singled them out with the supplication.

People have disputed who the "Family of Muhammad" (Al Muhammad) are. It was said: his community. This is the view of a group of the Companions of Muhammad, and of Malik and others. It was also said: the God-fearing among his community. They narrated a hadith: "The Family of Muhammad is every pious believer," narrated by al-Khallal, and Tammam in his al-Fawaʾid. A group of the companions of Ahmad and others argued with it, but it is a fabricated hadith. Upon this a group of the Sufis built the view that the Family of Muhammad are the elite of the saints, as mentioned by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi.

The correct view is that the Family of Muhammad are the People of his House. This is what is related from al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad, and it is the choice of al-Sharif Abu Jaʿfar and others. But are his wives among the People of his House? There are two views, which are two narrations from Ahmad. One of them: they are not among the People of the House, and this is related from Zayd ibn Arqam. The second, and it is the correct one: his wives are among his family. For it is established in the two Sahihs from the Prophet ﷺ that he taught them the prayer upon him: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, his wives and his offspring." Also, the wife of Abraham is among his family and People of his House, and the wife of Lot is among his family and People of his House, by the indication of the Qur'an. How then would the wives of Muhammad not be among his family and People of his House? Also, this verse indicates that they are among the People of his House, for otherwise mentioning that in the speech would have no meaning. As for the God-fearing of his community, they are his friends (awliya'), as is established in the Sahih that he said: "The family of so-and-so are not friends of mine; my friend is God and the righteous believers." So he made clear that his friends are the righteous believers. Likewise in another hadith: "My friends are the God-fearing, wherever they are and wherever they may be." God the Exalted has said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed God is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous believers﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4]. In the Sahih also from him: "I wished I had seen my brothers." They said: "Are we not your brothers?" He said: "No, you are my companions; my brothers are a people who will come after me, who believe in me though they have not seen me."

When this is the case, his friends are the God-fearing, and between him and them is the kinship of religion, faith and piety, and this religious kinship is greater than natural kinship. Closeness of hearts and spirits is greater than closeness of bodies. For this reason the best of creation were his God-fearing friends. As for his relatives, among them are believers and disbelievers, the righteous and the wicked. If some of them are excellent, such as ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, Jaʿfar, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, then he favored them for what is in them of faith and piety, and they are his friends in this respect, not merely by lineage.

So his friends are greater in rank than his family, and even if he sent blessings upon his family as a follower, that does not necessitate that they be superior to his friends upon whom he did not send blessings. For the prophets and messengers are among his friends, and they are superior to the People of his House, even if they did not enter the prayer with him as followers. The lesser may be singled out for a matter, and it does not follow that he is superior to the superior one. The proof of this is that his wives are among those upon whom he sends blessings, as is established in the two Sahihs. And it is established by the consensus of all people that the prophets are superior to all of them.

If it is said: suppose the Qur'an does not indicate the occurrence of what was intended of purification and removal of uncleanness; nevertheless, the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for it indicates its occurrence, for his supplication is answered. It is said: the point is that the Qur'an does not indicate what he claimed of establishing purity and removal of uncleanness, let alone that it indicates infallibility and the imamate. As for deriving proof from the hadith, that is another discussion.

Then we say in the second stance: suppose the Qur'an indicated their purity and the removal of their uncleanness. Just as an answered supplication must entail that the one prayed for be purified and that uncleanness be removed from them. But there is nothing in that which indicates infallibility from error. The proof of this is that God did not intend by what He commanded the wives of the Prophet ﷺ that no error should proceed from any one of them; for error is forgiven them and others. The context of the verse requires that He intends to remove from them the uncleanness, which is the filth, such as indecencies, and to purify them, a purification from indecencies and other sins.

Purification from sin is of two kinds, as in His saying: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 4], and His saying: ﴿Indeed they are people who purify themselves﴾ [al-Naml: 56]. He said in the verse: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30]. Purification from sins is either by the servant not doing it, or by repenting of it, as in His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]. What God commanded regarding purity at the outset and as an intention includes His prohibition of indecency; it does not include permission for it in any way. Rather, He, glory be to Him, forbids it and commands whoever commits it to repent from it. In the Sahih the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O God, separate me from my sins as You separated the east from the west. Wash me with snow, hail and cold water. O God, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth."

In sum, the term "rijs" (uncleanness) originally means filth. It is used to mean polytheism, as in His saying: ﴿So avoid the uncleanness of idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30], and it is used to mean forbidden impurities, such as foods and drinks, as in His saying: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is an uncleanness, or a sin﴾ [al-An'am: 145], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous altars and divining arrows are an uncleanness from the work of Satan﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90]. Removing that is removing all of it, and we know that God removed from those noble ones polytheism and impurities. The word "rijs" is general and requires that God removes all uncleanness. The Prophet ﷺ supplicated for that. As for His saying, "and purify them with a thorough purification," it is an unrestricted request for what is called purity.

Some people claim that this is unrestricted, so one instance of the instances of purity suffices for it. They say the same about His saying: ﴿So take warning, O people of insight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2] and similar. The verification is that it is a command to the thing called "consideration" when unrestricted, just as if it is said: "Honor this one," meaning: do with him what is called honoring when unrestricted. Likewise what is called consideration when unrestricted. A person is not called one who considers if he considers one story and leaves that in its counterpart. Similarly, one is not called pure, or one who purifies himself, or one who purifies, if he is purified from one thing while being defiled by its counterpart. The word "tahir" (pure) is like the word "tayyib" (good). God the Exalted said: ﴿Good things are for good people, and good people are for good things﴾ [al-Nur: 26], just as He said: ﴿Evil things are for evil people, and evil people are for evil things﴾ [al-Nur: 26]. It is related that he said to ʿAmmar: "Admit him. Welcome to the good, the perfumed one." This is also like the word "muttaqi" (God-fearing) and "muzakki" (one who purifies). God the Exalted said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams: 9], ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 10]. He said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103], and He said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [al-A'la: 14], and He said: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure, but God purifies whom He wills﴾ [al-Nur: 21]. It is not a condition for the God-fearing and their like that no sin occur from them, nor that they be protected from error and sins. For if this were so, there would be no God-fearing person in the community; rather, whoever repents from his sins enters among the God-fearing. As He said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴾ [al-Nisa': 31].

So the Prophet's ﷺ supplication that God purify them with a thorough purification is like his supplication that He cause them to grow, make them good, make them God-fearing, and the like. It is known that whoever has settled upon this matter is included in this, and the purity for which he prayed for them is not greater than what he prayed for himself. He said: "O God, purify me of my sins with snow, hail and cold water." Whoever's sin is forgiven or expiated, God has purified him of it with a thorough purification. But whoever dies soiled with his sins has not been purified of them in his life. It may be that part of the completeness of their purification is protecting them from charity, which is the filth of people. When the Prophet ﷺ supplicated with a supplication, God answered him according to the readiness of the recipient. When he asked forgiveness for the believing men and believing women, it does not follow that there is no sinful believer. For if this were the case, no believer would be punished, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Rather, God forgives this one through repentance, and that one through erasing good deeds, and God forgives this one many sins, and one thing follows another. In sum, the purification that God intended and for which the Prophet ﷺ prayed is not, by agreement, infallibility. For the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) hold that no one is infallible except the Prophet ﷺ. The Shi'ah say: no one is infallible except the Prophet ﷺ and the Imam.

Consensus holds that the infallibility (ʿiṣma) that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and to the Imam is denied of his wives, his daughters, and other women. Given this, the purification for which the four were supplicated cannot include the infallibility that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and, in their view, to the Imam. Therefore the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for him (ʿAlī) was not for this infallibility, either for ʿAlī or for anyone else. For he supplicated for four who were equal in this, so none of them was singled out by the supplication. Furthermore, supplicating for infallibility from sins is impossible according to the basic principles of the Qadariyya (the Qadarites, who deny divine predestination). Indeed, the same applies to purification as well. For voluntary acts, which are the performance of obligations and the avoidance of prohibitions, are, in their view, not within the power of the Lord, and He cannot make the servant obedient or disobedient, purified from sins or not purified. Thus, according to their principle, it is impossible to supplicate for anyone that He make him a doer of obligations and an avoider of prohibitions. What is within the power of the Lord, in their view, is a capacity suitable for good and evil, like a sword that is suitable for killing a Muslim or an unbeliever, or wealth that can be spent in obedience or in disobedience. Then the servant, by his own choice, does either good or evil by that capacity. This principle refutes their argument, and the hadith is a proof against them in refuting this principle, since the Prophet ﷺ supplicated for purification.

If they say: "What is meant by that is that He forgives them and does not hold them accountable," then that would be more clearly invalid than its indicating infallibility. Thus it becomes clear that the hadith provides them no proof whatsoever for the establishment of infallibility. Absolute infallibility (ʿiṣma), which is the performance of what is commanded and the avoidance of what is forbidden, is not, in their view, within God's power, and He cannot make anyone a doer of obedience or an avoider of disobedience, neither a prophet nor anyone else. In their view it is also impossible that One who knows that a person, if he lives, will obey Him by his own choice, not by God's help and guidance. This is among the things that demonstrate the contradiction in their statements on the matters of infallibility, as previously mentioned. Even if the existence of infallibility is assumed, we have already stated that infallibility is not a condition for the Imam, and there is consensus on the absence of infallibility in others. At that point, their argument is invalidated in every way. End.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[31–33] ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a generous provision.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire, but speak in a fair manner.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32] ﴿And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33]

﴿And whoever of you devotes herself﴾, i.e., continues in obedience. ﴿To God and His Messenger﴾, i.e., in performing the obligations and abstaining from what is forbidden and disliked. ﴿And does righteous deeds﴾, ﴿We will give her her reward twice over﴾, i.e., once for obedience and piety, and once for seeking the pleasure of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) through good character, pleasant companionship, and contentment. ﴿And We have prepared for her﴾, i.e., in addition to her doubled reward, in Paradise, or in it and in this world, ﴿a generous provision﴾, i.e., a good and pleasing one.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, do not be soft in speech﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., when addressing people. That is: do not answer with a soft, languid tone like the speech of women who arouse suspicion and of immoral women. ﴿Lest one in whose heart is a disease﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., doubt and debauchery, ﴿should feel desire﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32]. ﴿But speak in a fair manner﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., far from arousing the desire of one who harbors doubt, speak with seriousness and firmness, without softness; or, speak good words while being rough.

﴿And remain in your houses﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., stay and do not go out from them. It is from (waqara, yaqiru, waqaran), meaning "he became settled," or from (qarra, yaqirru, from the pattern of daraba), where the first of the two identical r's in (iqrarna, "remain") was dropped, and its vowel was transferred to the qaf, so the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with. This is supported by the reading of Nafi' and Asim with a fath (fatha), from (qarirtu, aqarru), from the pattern of ʿalima, which is a rare dialect. ﴿And do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., the display of women in the days of the first jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance, the age of disbelief). For there was no religion restraining them nor good manners holding them back. Tabarruj (display) has been explained as swaying and affected gait in walking, as showing adornment and what arouses a man's desire, as wearing thin clothing that does not conceal the body, and as displaying the beauty of the neck, necklaces, and earrings. All of this falls within the prohibition, because of the harm it contains and because it exposes one to a grave sin.

**Benefit:**
It has been said: "al-Ula" (the first) means "the former" in an unrestricted sense, without being limited to a particular time. Thus it is used as evidence for those who say that the first does not necessarily imply a second. In al-Iklil it is said: "This is the soundest view among scholars. So if someone says, 'The first child you bear, you are divorced,' she does not need to bear a second child." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "al-Ula is the ancient (jahiliyyah) that is called the jahiliyyah of the ignorant, from the time in which Abraham was born, or before it, until the time of Jesus. The jahiliyyah is what lies between Jesus and Muhammad, may the blessings of God be upon them both. It is also possible that the first jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of disbelief before Islam, and the other jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of sin and immorality within Islam. This is supported by what is narrated: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Abu Dhar, when he reproached a man for his mother, who was non-Arab: 'You are a man in whom there is jahiliyyah.'"

The meaning is a prohibition against them introducing a jahiliyyah into Islam, resembling the jahiliyyah of disbelief that came before it. ﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., by complying with their command and prohibition. Then He indicated that opposing them is impurity, which does not befit the virtue of the People of the House, in His words: ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., what He commanded you, forbade you, and admonished you about, is only out of fear of committing sins and eagerness to guard yourselves from them through piety. Thus the clause is causal, explaining His command and prohibition to them, as a fresh statement (isti'naf, a new clause).

(p. 4850) Al-Zamakhshari said: "He used 'impurity' (rijs) as a metaphor for sins, and 'purity' (tuhr) for piety, because the honor of one who commits abominations becomes soiled and defiled by them, just as his body becomes soiled by filth. As for virtuous deeds, the honor with them is pure and protected, like a clean garment. In this metaphor there is something that repels people of understanding from what God dislikes for His servants and forbade them, and encourages them toward what He is pleased with for them and commanded them to do."

﴿The People of the House﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] is in the accusative, either as a vocative or as a praise. What is meant by them is those whom the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) encompasses.

Ibn Kathir said: "This is an explicit text that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are included among the People of the House here, because they were the cause of the revelation of this verse, and the cause of revelation is undoubtedly included in it, either alone according to one opinion, or together with others according to the sound view. As for the statement of Ikrimah, that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically, and whoever wishes, I will challenge him on this, if what is meant is that they were the cause of the revelation and not others, then it is correct. But if what is meant is that they alone are intended to the exclusion of others, then there is room for examination, for there are hadiths indicating that what is meant is more general than that, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, then covered them with a cloak he had, and then said: 'These are my People of the House, so remove the impurity from them.'"

Ibn Kathir cited the chains of this hadith and those who transmitted it, but the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not authenticate it, and therefore did not include it. As for what Muslim narrated from Husayn ibn Sabrah, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Now then, O people! I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will answer. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of God, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of God and hold fast to it." He urged them to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and encouraged them toward it. Then he said: "And my People of the House. I remind you of God regarding my People of the House," and he said it three times. Husayn said to him: "And who are the People of his House, O Zayd? Are not his wives of his House?" He said: "His wives are of his House, but his People of the House are those for whom charity has been forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "The family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them" (p. 4851). Then what Zayd meant is his family who forbade charity; or it is that the People of the House is not meant as the wives alone, but they together with his family. Ibn Kathir said: "This is the more probable view, combining the Qur'an and the preceding hadiths, if they are sound, for there is some scrutiny regarding some of their chains."

Abu al-Su'ud said: "This, as you see, is a clear verse and a luminous proof that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are of his People of the House, decisively invalidating the view of the Shi'a in restricting the status of the People of the House to Fatimah, 'Ali, and their two sons, may God be pleased with them. As for what they cling to of the hadith of the cloak, and the Prophet's recitation of the verse after it, it indicates only that they are of the People of the House, not that others are not. And even if its indication of that were granted, it would not be considered, because it stands against an explicit text."

It remains that the Shi'a also cited the verse as evidence for the infallibility ('ismah) of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, and his imamate to the exclusion of others. Ibn al-Mutahhar al-Hilli, one of them, said: "In this verse is evidence of infallibility, with the emphasis of the word 'innama' (indeed, only), the inclusion of the lam in the predicate, and the specificity in the address with His words: ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], and others are not infallible, etc." Ibn Taymiyyah, may God have mercy on him, answered in (Minhaj al-Sunnah) with the words: "There is no evidence in this for their infallibility or their imamate. The verification of this is in two respects.

The first: His words ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] are like His words: ﴿God does not intend to place upon you any difficulty﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 6], and like His words: ﴿God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 185], and like His words: ﴿God intends to make clear to you and to guide you to the traditions of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness; and God is Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa': 26], ﴿And God intends to accept your repentance, while those who follow desires intend that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ [An-Nisa': 27]. For God's intention in these verses includes His love for that intended matter and His pleasure with it, and that He legislated it for the believers and commanded them to do it. It does not mean that He created this intended matter, nor that He decreed and determined it, nor that it will necessarily occur. The evidence for this is that after the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O God, these are my People of the House, so remove the impurity from them and purify them with complete purification.' He asked God on their behalf to remove the impurity and to purify them. Had the verse contained God's report that He had already removed the impurity from them and purified them, there would have been no need for request and supplication.

This is clearer according to the view of the Qadariyyah (the group who deny divine predestination in human acts). For their intention of God does not entail the existence of what is intended; rather He may intend what does not occur and what occurs He does not intend. So His being intending that does not indicate its occurrence.

This Rafidi (a term for the Shi'a) and his like are Qadariyyah, so how can they argue from His words ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] for the occurrence of what is intended? For according to them God intended the faith of everyone on the earth, yet His intention did not come to pass. As for the view of the affirmers (of divine decree), the verification in this matter is that the intention in the Book of God is of two kinds: a legislative, religious intention, which entails His love and His pleasure; and a universal, decreed intention, which entails His creation and His decree. The first is like these verses, and the second is like His words: ﴿Whomever God intends to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; and whomever He intends to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ [Al-An'am: 125], and the words of Noah: ﴿My advice will not benefit you if I wished to advise you, if God intends to lead you astray﴾ [Hud: 34].

Many of the affirmers and the Qadariyyah make intention one kind, just as they make intention and love one thing. Then the Qadariyyah negate His intention for what the legislation shows to be intended in the verses; for according to them, whatever is said to be intended does not necessarily exist. God has informed us that He intends to turn in forgiveness to the believers and to purify them, and among them are those who repented and those who did not repent, and among them are those who became pure and those who did not become pure. And if the verse indicates the occurrence of what He intended of purification and removal of impurity, it does not follow from the verse alone that what he claims is established."

Among the things that clarify this is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are explicitly mentioned in the verse, and the discussion concerns the command to purification through making it obligatory, the promise of reward for doing it, and the punishment for neglecting it. God the Exalted says: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold, and that is easy for God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30], up to His words: ﴿And obey God and His Messenger. God only intends to remove from you the uncleanness, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. The address is entirely to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and with them are the commands, prohibitions, promises and threats. However, when the benefit of this became clear, namely that it encompasses them and extends to others among the People of the House, the purification came with this address and other things, not exclusive to his wives. Rather, it encompasses all the People of the House, and ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the most particularly included in it over others. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ singled them out for supplication on their behalf. This is like His saying: ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 108], which was revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba, yet the ruling encompasses it and what is more worthy of it, namely the Mosque of Medina. This clarifies what is established in the Sahih from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about the mosque founded upon piety, and he said: "It is this mosque of mine." It is also established from him in the Sahih that he used to go to Quba every Saturday, on foot and riding, and he would stand in his mosque on Friday and come to Quba on Saturday, and both are founded upon piety. Likewise his wives, ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, are more particularly included in this than his wives; for this reason he singled them out with the supplication.

People have disputed who the "Family of Muhammad" (Al Muhammad) are. It was said: his community. This is the view of a group of the Companions of Muhammad, and of Malik and others. It was also said: the God-fearing among his community. They narrated a hadith: "The Family of Muhammad is every pious believer," narrated by al-Khallal, and Tammam in his al-Fawaʾid. A group of the companions of Ahmad and others argued with it, but it is a fabricated hadith. Upon this a group of the Sufis built the view that the Family of Muhammad are the elite of the saints, as mentioned by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi.

The correct view is that the Family of Muhammad are the People of his House. This is what is related from al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad, and it is the choice of al-Sharif Abu Jaʿfar and others. But are his wives among the People of his House? There are two views, which are two narrations from Ahmad. One of them: they are not among the People of the House, and this is related from Zayd ibn Arqam. The second, and it is the correct one: his wives are among his family. For it is established in the two Sahihs from the Prophet ﷺ that he taught them the prayer upon him: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, his wives and his offspring." Also, the wife of Abraham is among his family and People of his House, and the wife of Lot is among his family and People of his House, by the indication of the Qur'an. How then would the wives of Muhammad not be among his family and People of his House? Also, this verse indicates that they are among the People of his House, for otherwise mentioning that in the speech would have no meaning. As for the God-fearing of his community, they are his friends (awliya'), as is established in the Sahih that he said: "The family of so-and-so are not friends of mine; my friend is God and the righteous believers." So he made clear that his friends are the righteous believers. Likewise in another hadith: "My friends are the God-fearing, wherever they are and wherever they may be." God the Exalted has said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed God is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous believers﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4]. In the Sahih also from him: "I wished I had seen my brothers." They said: "Are we not your brothers?" He said: "No, you are my companions; my brothers are a people who will come after me, who believe in me though they have not seen me."

When this is the case, his friends are the God-fearing, and between him and them is the kinship of religion, faith and piety, and this religious kinship is greater than natural kinship. Closeness of hearts and spirits is greater than closeness of bodies. For this reason the best of creation were his God-fearing friends. As for his relatives, among them are believers and disbelievers, the righteous and the wicked. If some of them are excellent, such as ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, Jaʿfar, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, then he favored them for what is in them of faith and piety, and they are his friends in this respect, not merely by lineage.

So his friends are greater in rank than his family, and even if he sent blessings upon his family as a follower, that does not necessitate that they be superior to his friends upon whom he did not send blessings. For the prophets and messengers are among his friends, and they are superior to the People of his House, even if they did not enter the prayer with him as followers. The lesser may be singled out for a matter, and it does not follow that he is superior to the superior one. The proof of this is that his wives are among those upon whom he sends blessings, as is established in the two Sahihs. And it is established by the consensus of all people that the prophets are superior to all of them.

If it is said: suppose the Qur'an does not indicate the occurrence of what was intended of purification and removal of uncleanness; nevertheless, the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for it indicates its occurrence, for his supplication is answered. It is said: the point is that the Qur'an does not indicate what he claimed of establishing purity and removal of uncleanness, let alone that it indicates infallibility and the imamate. As for deriving proof from the hadith, that is another discussion.

Then we say in the second stance: suppose the Qur'an indicated their purity and the removal of their uncleanness. Just as an answered supplication must entail that the one prayed for be purified and that uncleanness be removed from them. But there is nothing in that which indicates infallibility from error. The proof of this is that God did not intend by what He commanded the wives of the Prophet ﷺ that no error should proceed from any one of them; for error is forgiven them and others. The context of the verse requires that He intends to remove from them the uncleanness, which is the filth, such as indecencies, and to purify them, a purification from indecencies and other sins.

Purification from sin is of two kinds, as in His saying: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 4], and His saying: ﴿Indeed they are people who purify themselves﴾ [al-Naml: 56]. He said in the verse: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30]. Purification from sins is either by the servant not doing it, or by repenting of it, as in His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]. What God commanded regarding purity at the outset and as an intention includes His prohibition of indecency; it does not include permission for it in any way. Rather, He, glory be to Him, forbids it and commands whoever commits it to repent from it. In the Sahih the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O God, separate me from my sins as You separated the east from the west. Wash me with snow, hail and cold water. O God, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth."

In sum, the term "rijs" (uncleanness) originally means filth. It is used to mean polytheism, as in His saying: ﴿So avoid the uncleanness of idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30], and it is used to mean forbidden impurities, such as foods and drinks, as in His saying: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is an uncleanness, or a sin﴾ [al-An'am: 145], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous altars and divining arrows are an uncleanness from the work of Satan﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90]. Removing that is removing all of it, and we know that God removed from those noble ones polytheism and impurities. The word "rijs" is general and requires that God removes all uncleanness. The Prophet ﷺ supplicated for that. As for His saying, "and purify them with a thorough purification," it is an unrestricted request for what is called purity.

Some people claim that this is unrestricted, so one instance of the instances of purity suffices for it. They say the same about His saying: ﴿So take warning, O people of insight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2] and similar. The verification is that it is a command to the thing called "consideration" when unrestricted, just as if it is said: "Honor this one," meaning: do with him what is called honoring when unrestricted. Likewise what is called consideration when unrestricted. A person is not called one who considers if he considers one story and leaves that in its counterpart. Similarly, one is not called pure, or one who purifies himself, or one who purifies, if he is purified from one thing while being defiled by its counterpart. The word "tahir" (pure) is like the word "tayyib" (good). God the Exalted said: ﴿Good things are for good people, and good people are for good things﴾ [al-Nur: 26], just as He said: ﴿Evil things are for evil people, and evil people are for evil things﴾ [al-Nur: 26]. It is related that he said to ʿAmmar: "Admit him. Welcome to the good, the perfumed one." This is also like the word "muttaqi" (God-fearing) and "muzakki" (one who purifies). God the Exalted said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams: 9], ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 10]. He said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103], and He said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [al-A'la: 14], and He said: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure, but God purifies whom He wills﴾ [al-Nur: 21]. It is not a condition for the God-fearing and their like that no sin occur from them, nor that they be protected from error and sins. For if this were so, there would be no God-fearing person in the community; rather, whoever repents from his sins enters among the God-fearing. As He said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴾ [al-Nisa': 31].

So the Prophet's ﷺ supplication that God purify them with a thorough purification is like his supplication that He cause them to grow, make them good, make them God-fearing, and the like. It is known that whoever has settled upon this matter is included in this, and the purity for which he prayed for them is not greater than what he prayed for himself. He said: "O God, purify me of my sins with snow, hail and cold water." Whoever's sin is forgiven or expiated, God has purified him of it with a thorough purification. But whoever dies soiled with his sins has not been purified of them in his life. It may be that part of the completeness of their purification is protecting them from charity, which is the filth of people. When the Prophet ﷺ supplicated with a supplication, God answered him according to the readiness of the recipient. When he asked forgiveness for the believing men and believing women, it does not follow that there is no sinful believer. For if this were the case, no believer would be punished, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Rather, God forgives this one through repentance, and that one through erasing good deeds, and God forgives this one many sins, and one thing follows another. In sum, the purification that God intended and for which the Prophet ﷺ prayed is not, by agreement, infallibility. For the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) hold that no one is infallible except the Prophet ﷺ. The Shi'ah say: no one is infallible except the Prophet ﷺ and the Imam.

Consensus holds that the infallibility (ʿiṣma) that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and to the Imam is denied of his wives, his daughters, and other women. Given this, the purification for which the four were supplicated cannot include the infallibility that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and, in their view, to the Imam. Therefore the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for him (ʿAlī) was not for this infallibility, either for ʿAlī or for anyone else. For he supplicated for four who were equal in this, so none of them was singled out by the supplication. Furthermore, supplicating for infallibility from sins is impossible according to the basic principles of the Qadariyya (the Qadarites, who deny divine predestination). Indeed, the same applies to purification as well. For voluntary acts, which are the performance of obligations and the avoidance of prohibitions, are, in their view, not within the power of the Lord, and He cannot make the servant obedient or disobedient, purified from sins or not purified. Thus, according to their principle, it is impossible to supplicate for anyone that He make him a doer of obligations and an avoider of prohibitions. What is within the power of the Lord, in their view, is a capacity suitable for good and evil, like a sword that is suitable for killing a Muslim or an unbeliever, or wealth that can be spent in obedience or in disobedience. Then the servant, by his own choice, does either good or evil by that capacity. This principle refutes their argument, and the hadith is a proof against them in refuting this principle, since the Prophet ﷺ supplicated for purification.

If they say: "What is meant by that is that He forgives them and does not hold them accountable," then that would be more clearly invalid than its indicating infallibility. Thus it becomes clear that the hadith provides them no proof whatsoever for the establishment of infallibility. Absolute infallibility (ʿiṣma), which is the performance of what is commanded and the avoidance of what is forbidden, is not, in their view, within God's power, and He cannot make anyone a doer of obedience or an avoider of disobedience, neither a prophet nor anyone else. In their view it is also impossible that One who knows that a person, if he lives, will obey Him by his own choice, not by God's help and guidance. This is among the things that demonstrate the contradiction in their statements on the matters of infallibility, as previously mentioned. Even if the existence of infallibility is assumed, we have already stated that infallibility is not a condition for the Imam, and there is consensus on the absence of infallibility in others. At that point, their argument is invalidated in every way. End.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[31–33] ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a generous provision.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire, but speak in a fair manner.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32] ﴿And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33]

﴿And whoever of you devotes herself﴾, i.e., continues in obedience. ﴿To God and His Messenger﴾, i.e., in performing the obligations and abstaining from what is forbidden and disliked. ﴿And does righteous deeds﴾, ﴿We will give her her reward twice over﴾, i.e., once for obedience and piety, and once for seeking the pleasure of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) through good character, pleasant companionship, and contentment. ﴿And We have prepared for her﴾, i.e., in addition to her doubled reward, in Paradise, or in it and in this world, ﴿a generous provision﴾, i.e., a good and pleasing one.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, do not be soft in speech﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., when addressing people. That is: do not answer with a soft, languid tone like the speech of women who arouse suspicion and of immoral women. ﴿Lest one in whose heart is a disease﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., doubt and debauchery, ﴿should feel desire﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32]. ﴿But speak in a fair manner﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32], i.e., far from arousing the desire of one who harbors doubt, speak with seriousness and firmness, without softness; or, speak good words while being rough.

﴿And remain in your houses﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., stay and do not go out from them. It is from (waqara, yaqiru, waqaran), meaning "he became settled," or from (qarra, yaqirru, from the pattern of daraba), where the first of the two identical r's in (iqrarna, "remain") was dropped, and its vowel was transferred to the qaf, so the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with. This is supported by the reading of Nafi' and Asim with a fath (fatha), from (qarirtu, aqarru), from the pattern of ʿalima, which is a rare dialect. ﴿And do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., the display of women in the days of the first jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance, the age of disbelief). For there was no religion restraining them nor good manners holding them back. Tabarruj (display) has been explained as swaying and affected gait in walking, as showing adornment and what arouses a man's desire, as wearing thin clothing that does not conceal the body, and as displaying the beauty of the neck, necklaces, and earrings. All of this falls within the prohibition, because of the harm it contains and because it exposes one to a grave sin.

**Benefit:**
It has been said: "al-Ula" (the first) means "the former" in an unrestricted sense, without being limited to a particular time. Thus it is used as evidence for those who say that the first does not necessarily imply a second. In al-Iklil it is said: "This is the soundest view among scholars. So if someone says, 'The first child you bear, you are divorced,' she does not need to bear a second child." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "al-Ula is the ancient (jahiliyyah) that is called the jahiliyyah of the ignorant, from the time in which Abraham was born, or before it, until the time of Jesus. The jahiliyyah is what lies between Jesus and Muhammad, may the blessings of God be upon them both. It is also possible that the first jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of disbelief before Islam, and the other jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of sin and immorality within Islam. This is supported by what is narrated: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Abu Dhar, when he reproached a man for his mother, who was non-Arab: 'You are a man in whom there is jahiliyyah.'"

The meaning is a prohibition against them introducing a jahiliyyah into Islam, resembling the jahiliyyah of disbelief that came before it. ﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., by complying with their command and prohibition. Then He indicated that opposing them is impurity, which does not befit the virtue of the People of the House, in His words: ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], i.e., what He commanded you, forbade you, and admonished you about, is only out of fear of committing sins and eagerness to guard yourselves from them through piety. Thus the clause is causal, explaining His command and prohibition to them, as a fresh statement (isti'naf, a new clause).

(p. 4850) Al-Zamakhshari said: "He used 'impurity' (rijs) as a metaphor for sins, and 'purity' (tuhr) for piety, because the honor of one who commits abominations becomes soiled and defiled by them, just as his body becomes soiled by filth. As for virtuous deeds, the honor with them is pure and protected, like a clean garment. In this metaphor there is something that repels people of understanding from what God dislikes for His servants and forbade them, and encourages them toward what He is pleased with for them and commanded them to do."

﴿The People of the House﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] is in the accusative, either as a vocative or as a praise. What is meant by them is those whom the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) encompasses.

Ibn Kathir said: "This is an explicit text that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are included among the People of the House here, because they were the cause of the revelation of this verse, and the cause of revelation is undoubtedly included in it, either alone according to one opinion, or together with others according to the sound view. As for the statement of Ikrimah, that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically, and whoever wishes, I will challenge him on this, if what is meant is that they were the cause of the revelation and not others, then it is correct. But if what is meant is that they alone are intended to the exclusion of others, then there is room for examination, for there are hadiths indicating that what is meant is more general than that, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, then covered them with a cloak he had, and then said: 'These are my People of the House, so remove the impurity from them.'"

Ibn Kathir cited the chains of this hadith and those who transmitted it, but the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not authenticate it, and therefore did not include it. As for what Muslim narrated from Husayn ibn Sabrah, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Now then, O people! I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will answer. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of God, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of God and hold fast to it." He urged them to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and encouraged them toward it. Then he said: "And my People of the House. I remind you of God regarding my People of the House," and he said it three times. Husayn said to him: "And who are the People of his House, O Zayd? Are not his wives of his House?" He said: "His wives are of his House, but his People of the House are those for whom charity has been forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "The family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them" (p. 4851). Then what Zayd meant is his family who forbade charity; or it is that the People of the House is not meant as the wives alone, but they together with his family. Ibn Kathir said: "This is the more probable view, combining the Qur'an and the preceding hadiths, if they are sound, for there is some scrutiny regarding some of their chains."

Abu al-Su'ud said: "This, as you see, is a clear verse and a luminous proof that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are of his People of the House, decisively invalidating the view of the Shi'a in restricting the status of the People of the House to Fatimah, 'Ali, and their two sons, may God be pleased with them. As for what they cling to of the hadith of the cloak, and the Prophet's recitation of the verse after it, it indicates only that they are of the People of the House, not that others are not. And even if its indication of that were granted, it would not be considered, because it stands against an explicit text."

It remains that the Shi'a also cited the verse as evidence for the infallibility ('ismah) of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, and his imamate to the exclusion of others. Ibn al-Mutahhar al-Hilli, one of them, said: "In this verse is evidence of infallibility, with the emphasis of the word 'innama' (indeed, only), the inclusion of the lam in the predicate, and the specificity in the address with His words: ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], and others are not infallible, etc." Ibn Taymiyyah, may God have mercy on him, answered in (Minhaj al-Sunnah) with the words: "There is no evidence in this for their infallibility or their imamate. The verification of this is in two respects.

The first: His words ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] are like His words: ﴿God does not intend to place upon you any difficulty﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 6], and like His words: ﴿God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 185], and like His words: ﴿God intends to make clear to you and to guide you to the traditions of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness; and God is Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa': 26], ﴿And God intends to accept your repentance, while those who follow desires intend that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ [An-Nisa': 27]. For God's intention in these verses includes His love for that intended matter and His pleasure with it, and that He legislated it for the believers and commanded them to do it. It does not mean that He created this intended matter, nor that He decreed and determined it, nor that it will necessarily occur. The evidence for this is that after the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O God, these are my People of the House, so remove the impurity from them and purify them with complete purification.' He asked God on their behalf to remove the impurity and to purify them. Had the verse contained God's report that He had already removed the impurity from them and purified them, there would have been no need for request and supplication.

This is clearer according to the view of the Qadariyyah (the group who deny divine predestination in human acts). For their intention of God does not entail the existence of what is intended; rather He may intend what does not occur and what occurs He does not intend. So His being intending that does not indicate its occurrence.

This Rafidi (a term for the Shi'a) and his like are Qadariyyah, so how can they argue from His words ﴿Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33] for the occurrence of what is intended? For according to them God intended the faith of everyone on the earth, yet His intention did not come to pass. As for the view of the affirmers (of divine decree), the verification in this matter is that the intention in the Book of God is of two kinds: a legislative, religious intention, which entails His love and His pleasure; and a universal, decreed intention, which entails His creation and His decree. The first is like these verses, and the second is like His words: ﴿Whomever God intends to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; and whomever He intends to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ [Al-An'am: 125], and the words of Noah: ﴿My advice will not benefit you if I wished to advise you, if God intends to lead you astray﴾ [Hud: 34].

Many of the affirmers and the Qadariyyah make intention one kind, just as they make intention and love one thing. Then the Qadariyyah negate His intention for what the legislation shows to be intended in the verses; for according to them, whatever is said to be intended does not necessarily exist. God has informed us that He intends to turn in forgiveness to the believers and to purify them, and among them are those who repented and those who did not repent, and among them are those who became pure and those who did not become pure. And if the verse indicates the occurrence of what He intended of purification and removal of impurity, it does not follow from the verse alone that what he claims is established."

Among the things that clarify this is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are explicitly mentioned in the verse, and the discussion concerns the command to purification through making it obligatory, the promise of reward for doing it, and the punishment for neglecting it. God the Exalted says: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold, and that is easy for God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30], up to His words: ﴿And obey God and His Messenger. God only intends to remove from you the uncleanness, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. The address is entirely to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and with them are the commands, prohibitions, promises and threats. However, when the benefit of this became clear, namely that it encompasses them and extends to others among the People of the House, the purification came with this address and other things, not exclusive to his wives. Rather, it encompasses all the People of the House, and ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the most particularly included in it over others. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ singled them out for supplication on their behalf. This is like His saying: ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 108], which was revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba, yet the ruling encompasses it and what is more worthy of it, namely the Mosque of Medina. This clarifies what is established in the Sahih from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about the mosque founded upon piety, and he said: "It is this mosque of mine." It is also established from him in the Sahih that he used to go to Quba every Saturday, on foot and riding, and he would stand in his mosque on Friday and come to Quba on Saturday, and both are founded upon piety. Likewise his wives, ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, are more particularly included in this than his wives; for this reason he singled them out with the supplication.

People have disputed who the "Family of Muhammad" (Al Muhammad) are. It was said: his community. This is the view of a group of the Companions of Muhammad, and of Malik and others. It was also said: the God-fearing among his community. They narrated a hadith: "The Family of Muhammad is every pious believer," narrated by al-Khallal, and Tammam in his al-Fawaʾid. A group of the companions of Ahmad and others argued with it, but it is a fabricated hadith. Upon this a group of the Sufis built the view that the Family of Muhammad are the elite of the saints, as mentioned by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi.

The correct view is that the Family of Muhammad are the People of his House. This is what is related from al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad, and it is the choice of al-Sharif Abu Jaʿfar and others. But are his wives among the People of his House? There are two views, which are two narrations from Ahmad. One of them: they are not among the People of the House, and this is related from Zayd ibn Arqam. The second, and it is the correct one: his wives are among his family. For it is established in the two Sahihs from the Prophet ﷺ that he taught them the prayer upon him: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, his wives and his offspring." Also, the wife of Abraham is among his family and People of his House, and the wife of Lot is among his family and People of his House, by the indication of the Qur'an. How then would the wives of Muhammad not be among his family and People of his House? Also, this verse indicates that they are among the People of his House, for otherwise mentioning that in the speech would have no meaning. As for the God-fearing of his community, they are his friends (awliya'), as is established in the Sahih that he said: "The family of so-and-so are not friends of mine; my friend is God and the righteous believers." So he made clear that his friends are the righteous believers. Likewise in another hadith: "My friends are the God-fearing, wherever they are and wherever they may be." God the Exalted has said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed God is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous believers﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4]. In the Sahih also from him: "I wished I had seen my brothers." They said: "Are we not your brothers?" He said: "No, you are my companions; my brothers are a people who will come after me, who believe in me though they have not seen me."

When this is the case, his friends are the God-fearing, and between him and them is the kinship of religion, faith and piety, and this religious kinship is greater than natural kinship. Closeness of hearts and spirits is greater than closeness of bodies. For this reason the best of creation were his God-fearing friends. As for his relatives, among them are believers and disbelievers, the righteous and the wicked. If some of them are excellent, such as ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, Jaʿfar, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, then he favored them for what is in them of faith and piety, and they are his friends in this respect, not merely by lineage.

So his friends are greater in rank than his family, and even if he sent blessings upon his family as a follower, that does not necessitate that they be superior to his friends upon whom he did not send blessings. For the prophets and messengers are among his friends, and they are superior to the People of his House, even if they did not enter the prayer with him as followers. The lesser may be singled out for a matter, and it does not follow that he is superior to the superior one. The proof of this is that his wives are among those upon whom he sends blessings, as is established in the two Sahihs. And it is established by the consensus of all people that the prophets are superior to all of them.

If it is said: suppose the Qur'an does not indicate the occurrence of what was intended of purification and removal of uncleanness; nevertheless, the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for it indicates its occurrence, for his supplication is answered. It is said: the point is that the Qur'an does not indicate what he claimed of establishing purity and removal of uncleanness, let alone that it indicates infallibility and the imamate. As for deriving proof from the hadith, that is another discussion.

Then we say in the second stance: suppose the Qur'an indicated their purity and the removal of their uncleanness. Just as an answered supplication must entail that the one prayed for be purified and that uncleanness be removed from them. But there is nothing in that which indicates infallibility from error. The proof of this is that God did not intend by what He commanded the wives of the Prophet ﷺ that no error should proceed from any one of them; for error is forgiven them and others. The context of the verse requires that He intends to remove from them the uncleanness, which is the filth, such as indecencies, and to purify them, a purification from indecencies and other sins.

Purification from sin is of two kinds, as in His saying: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 4], and His saying: ﴿Indeed they are people who purify themselves﴾ [al-Naml: 56]. He said in the verse: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30]. Purification from sins is either by the servant not doing it, or by repenting of it, as in His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]. What God commanded regarding purity at the outset and as an intention includes His prohibition of indecency; it does not include permission for it in any way. Rather, He, glory be to Him, forbids it and commands whoever commits it to repent from it. In the Sahih the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O God, separate me from my sins as You separated the east from the west. Wash me with snow, hail and cold water. O God, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth."

In sum, the term "rijs" (uncleanness) originally means filth. It is used to mean polytheism, as in His saying: ﴿So avoid the uncleanness of idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30], and it is used to mean forbidden impurities, such as foods and drinks, as in His saying: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is an uncleanness, or a sin﴾ [al-An'am: 145], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous altars and divining arrows are an uncleanness from the work of Satan﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90]. Removing that is removing all of it, and we know that God removed from those noble ones polytheism and impurities. The word "rijs" is general and requires that God removes all uncleanness. The Prophet ﷺ supplicated for that. As for His saying, "and purify them with a thorough purification," it is an unrestricted request for what is called purity.

Some people claim that this is unrestricted, so one instance of the instances of purity suffices for it. They say the same about His saying: ﴿So take warning, O people of insight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2] and similar. The verification is that it is a command to the thing called "consideration" when unrestricted, just as if it is said: "Honor this one," meaning: do with him what is called honoring when unrestricted. Likewise what is called consideration when unrestricted. A person is not called one who considers if he considers one story and leaves that in its counterpart. Similarly, one is not called pure, or one who purifies himself, or one who purifies, if he is purified from one thing while being defiled by its counterpart. The word "tahir" (pure) is like the word "tayyib" (good). God the Exalted said: ﴿Good things are for good people, and good people are for good things﴾ [al-Nur: 26], just as He said: ﴿Evil things are for evil people, and evil people are for evil things﴾ [al-Nur: 26]. It is related that he said to ʿAmmar: "Admit him. Welcome to the good, the perfumed one." This is also like the word "muttaqi" (God-fearing) and "muzakki" (one who purifies). God the Exalted said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams: 9], ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 10]. He said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103], and He said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [al-A'la: 14], and He said: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure, but God purifies whom He wills﴾ [al-Nur: 21]. It is not a condition for the God-fearing and their like that no sin occur from them, nor that they be protected from error and sins. For if this were so, there would be no God-fearing person in the community; rather, whoever repents from his sins enters among the God-fearing. As He said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴾ [al-Nisa': 31].

So the Prophet's ﷺ supplication that God purify them with a thorough purification is like his supplication that He cause them to grow, make them good, make them God-fearing, and the like. It is known that whoever has settled upon this matter is included in this, and the purity for which he prayed for them is not greater than what he prayed for himself. He said: "O God, purify me of my sins with snow, hail and cold water." Whoever's sin is forgiven or expiated, God has purified him of it with a thorough purification. But whoever dies soiled with his sins has not been purified of them in his life. It may be that part of the completeness of their purification is protecting them from charity, which is the filth of people. When the Prophet ﷺ supplicated with a supplication, God answered him according to the readiness of the recipient. When he asked forgiveness for the believing men and believing women, it does not follow that there is no sinful believer. For if this were the case, no believer would be punished, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Rather, God forgives this one through repentance, and that one through erasing good deeds, and God forgives this one many sins, and one thing follows another. In sum, the purification that God intended and for which the Prophet ﷺ prayed is not, by agreement, infallibility. For the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) hold that no one is infallible except the Prophet ﷺ. The Shi'ah say: no one is infallible except the Prophet ﷺ and the Imam.

Consensus holds that the infallibility (ʿiṣma) that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and to the Imam is denied of his wives, his daughters, and other women. Given this, the purification for which the four were supplicated cannot include the infallibility that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and, in their view, to the Imam. Therefore the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for him (ʿAlī) was not for this infallibility, either for ʿAlī or for anyone else. For he supplicated for four who were equal in this, so none of them was singled out by the supplication. Furthermore, supplicating for infallibility from sins is impossible according to the basic principles of the Qadariyya (the Qadarites, who deny divine predestination). Indeed, the same applies to purification as well. For voluntary acts, which are the performance of obligations and the avoidance of prohibitions, are, in their view, not within the power of the Lord, and He cannot make the servant obedient or disobedient, purified from sins or not purified. Thus, according to their principle, it is impossible to supplicate for anyone that He make him a doer of obligations and an avoider of prohibitions. What is within the power of the Lord, in their view, is a capacity suitable for good and evil, like a sword that is suitable for killing a Muslim or an unbeliever, or wealth that can be spent in obedience or in disobedience. Then the servant, by his own choice, does either good or evil by that capacity. This principle refutes their argument, and the hadith is a proof against them in refuting this principle, since the Prophet ﷺ supplicated for purification.

If they say: "What is meant by that is that He forgives them and does not hold them accountable," then that would be more clearly invalid than its indicating infallibility. Thus it becomes clear that the hadith provides them no proof whatsoever for the establishment of infallibility. Absolute infallibility (ʿiṣma), which is the performance of what is commanded and the avoidance of what is forbidden, is not, in their view, within God's power, and He cannot make anyone a doer of obedience or an avoider of disobedience, neither a prophet nor anyone else. In their view it is also impossible that One who knows that a person, if he lives, will obey Him by his own choice, not by God's help and guidance. This is among the things that demonstrate the contradiction in their statements on the matters of infallibility, as previously mentioned. Even if the existence of infallibility is assumed, we have already stated that infallibility is not a condition for the Imam, and there is consensus on the absence of infallibility in others. At that point, their argument is invalidated in every way. End.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 33, Verse 34:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾ is a command to them to remember, and not to neglect, what is recited in their houses from the verses of His Book, the Exalted, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ), the two of which contain the life of souls, their happiness, and the foundation of good manners and morals. Remembering this requires forming a conception of its greatness, its status, and the fruit of its benefit. That leads to acting upon it. So whoever interprets "remember" (udhkurna) as "act upon it" (u'malna bihi) means that by naming the cause (sabab) he expresses the effect (musabbab). It is also permissible that the meaning is: remember this blessing, in that you have been made the people of the House of Prophethood and the place of the descent of revelation, which necessitates the strengthening of faith and eagerness for obedience, as an incitement to refrain from what is forbidden and to comply with what you have been charged with.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The mention of recitation in the houses, rather than descent in them, although it was the place of the descent of revelation, is because recitation covers all the verses and occurs in every house, and its repetition necessitates their ability to remember and to remind. This differs from descent, and the reciter is not specified, so that the recitation of Jibril (ﷺ), the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ), their recitation, and the recitation of others is included, in teaching and learning. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, that is: He knows and arranges what is good in the religion, and for this reason He commands and prohibits.

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[35] ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them, and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, that is, those who submit outwardly to the judgment of Allah, both men and women. ﴿And the believing men and believing women﴾, that is, those who affirm in the heart what must be affirmed. ﴿And the devoutly obedient (qanitin) men and devoutly obedient women﴾, that is, by persisting in obedience with the limbs in acts of worship. ﴿And the truthful men and truthful women﴾, in speech by avoiding falsehood, and in action by devoting sincerity purely to His Face, exalted is He, so that there is no showing-off (riya') in their obedience. ﴿And the patient men and patient women﴾, that is, patient in hardship, adversity and calamities, and in performing worship and persevering in it. ﴿And the humble men and humble women﴾, that is, those who humble themselves before Allah with their hearts and limbs. And (al-khushu'): tranquility, calm, deliberateness, dignity and humility; what impels it is fear of Him, exalted is He, and watchfulness over Him. ﴿And the charitable men and charitable women﴾, that is, by doing good to the poor and the destitute who have no earnings and no one earning for them, so they give from the surplus of their wealth, in obedience to Allah, in kindness to His creation, and to complete the humility. ﴿And the fasting men and fasting women﴾, that is, those who carry out what was required of them of fasting, which bequeaths piety and compassion toward one who suffers hunger and endures poverty patiently. ﴿And the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them﴾, that is, from exposing them and displaying them, out of modesty and restraint from the sources of forbidden desire, or from what is unlawful and immoral. ﴿And the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him﴾, that is, with their hearts and tongues. ﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness﴾, that is, because of the good deeds mentioned that they did, forgiveness for the minor sins they committed, since these are expiated thereby. ﴿And a great reward﴾, that is, abundant reward in Paradise.

And His statement, exalted is He:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 33, verse 36:

(p-4861) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[36] ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman﴾ means: it is not valid for them both. ﴿When Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair﴾ means: Allah and His Messenger have issued a decree concerning them, that they should choose for themselves something other than what has been decreed for them, and oppose the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger, their decree, and disobey them both, because of the sin in that.
