As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, in what they have commanded or forbidden: ﴿has certainly strayed into clear error﴾, that is, he has deviated from the straight path and taken other than guidance and right direction.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed her to Zayd ibn Harithah, but she refused because he was a freedman, not her equal in nobility. Then the verse was revealed, and she consented and married him.

Al-Mahayimi said: The apparent meaning is that the proposal was by way of obligation. It is possible that it was not by way of obligation, but considering shame in the face of the proposal of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is disobedience, because it involves preferring the words of the people of custom over the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), even though, in reality, his words are the words of Allah.

Some of them said: The revelation only counted her refusal as disobedience, as though He had compelled her into his marriage, because of the benefit Allah brought about for her and for the Muslims in that, namely the demolition of the prohibition of the wife of the adopted son, which was widespread in the Jahiliyyah, as its context will come later.

It has also been mentioned that it was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. She was the first woman to emigrate after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and she offered herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he married her to Zayd, that is, after his separation from Zaynab. She was displeased, so the verse was revealed, and she consented.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Anas, who said: (p-4862) "The Prophet (ﷺ) proposed on behalf of Julaybib, may Allah be pleased with him, to a woman of the Ansar from her father. He said: 'Let me consult her mother.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Yes, then.' He said: So the man went to his wife and mentioned that to her, and she refused with the utmost refusal. The girl said: Do you want to reject the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? If he has approved him for you, then marry him to him. He said: So it was as though she had dispelled her parents' concern, and they both said: She has spoken the truth. So her father went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: If you have approved of him, then we have approved of him. He (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed I have approved of him.' He said: So he married her. Then he went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) on a campaign, and was killed. Around him were seen some polytheists whom he had killed. Anas said: I certainly saw her, and she was among the most generous households in Madinah. In another narration: 'There was no widow among the Ansar more generous than her.'"

The hafiz Ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned in (al-Isti'ab) that when the girl said, in her seclusion: Do you reject the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman﴾.

There is no doubt that the verse includes what has been mentioned and other things, except that the connection of this verse with the story of Zayd and his wife, which follows, supports that it was revealed concerning his wife Zaynab, for the coherence of the order of the verses then, and because this verse appears as a prelude to this glorious story.

We have previously stated several times that the meaning of their saying "the verse was revealed concerning such-and-such" is that it is among what it encompasses by the generality of its context. That is why Tawus asked Ibn 'Abbas about two rak'ahs after the 'Asr prayer, and he forbade him, and recited this verse to him.

Ibn Kathir said: This verse is general in all matters. When Allah and His Messenger decide something, it is not permissible for anyone to oppose it, and no one has any choice, opinion, or saying in it, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no resistance against what you have decided and submit with full acceptance﴾ [An-Nisa: 65]. And in the hadith: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought." Therefore He emphasized the opposition to that, saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger (p-4863) has certainly strayed into clear error﴾, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then let those beware who oppose the Messenger's order, lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment strike them﴾ [An-Nur: 63].

Nuances:

First: They said, regarding the previous narrations: The mention of Allah in the verse, although the one who commands them is the Messenger (ﷺ), is to indicate that he holds a station from Allah such that his commands are counted as the commands of Allah the Exalted, or that since what he does is by His command, for he does not speak from desire, the Name of Majesty was mentioned and placed first to indicate that. End.

This is a standing upon what has been narrated; otherwise, the apparent meaning of the verse covers the case where Allah decrees by His Book and His Messenger by his Sunnah.

Second: "Al-khiyarah" (choice) here is a verbal noun (masdar), and they mentioned that no verbal noun on its pattern has come except "tiyarah."

Third: The plural of the first pronoun, which is "lahum," is due to the generality of "believing man" and "believing woman," inasmuch as they are in the context of negation. Al-Shihab said: Its generality is taken into account, even though the occasion of its revelation was specific, to repel the notion that it is restricted to the occasion of revelation, or to indicate that just as what they chose is not valid when alone, it is not valid when together either, lest one suppose that collectivity has a strength that validates it. End.

The plural of the second, which is the pronoun in "amrihim," although the one meant is the Messenger (ﷺ), or it refers to him and to Allah the Exalted, is for exaltation. This is what al-Qadi and others pointed out. Yet it does not appear that its returning to what the first referred to is impossible, with preference given to it for not breaking the reference, on the basis that the meaning is: arising from their affair. The meaning is their prior motives toward choosing what opposes what Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) commanded, or the meaning is choice in some part of their affair, that is, their motives. This was rejected, on the grounds that it is of little benefit, since it is necessary that choice arises from their motives... or occurs in their affairs. This is clear and needs no explanation. In contrast is when the meaning is instead of (p-4864) his command which he (ﷺ) decreed, or going beyond his command, for emphasizing and confirming the negation. This is what prevents its return to what the first referred to.

Al-Shihab said: This is a fine statement. Then He, exalted is He, pointed to what He bestowed upon the Muslims by demolishing the prohibition of the wife of the adopted son, which was widespread in the Jahiliyyah, through what occurred between Zayd, the adopted son of the Prophet (ﷺ), and his wife by way of separation, then His, exalted is He, marrying her to His Prophet (ﷺ), removing the difficulty in it. So He, exalted is He, said:

The discussion of the Lord's words:

[37–39] ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need of her, We married her to you so that there would be upon the believers no discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.﴾ ﴿There is not upon the Prophet any discomfort in what Allah has enjoined upon him. [That is] the established practice of Allah concerning those who passed on before, and ever is the command of Allah a decree determined.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 38] ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 39].

﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor﴾ i.e., with Islam and following the Prophet ﷺ, and he was Zayd ibn Harithah; ﴿and you bestowed favor upon him﴾ i.e., with manumission and freedom, and by singling him out for guardianship and love, and by marrying him to your paternal aunt's daughter, Zaynab bint Jahsh.

(p-4865) Ibn Kathir said: He was a leader of great standing and lofty rank, beloved to the Prophet ﷺ, and he was called "al-Hibb" (the beloved). And his son Usamah was called "al-Hibb ibn al-Hibb" (the beloved, son of the beloved). ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never sent him on an expedition without appointing him over them, and had he lived after him, he would have made him his successor. Related by Imam Ahmad. ﴿Keep your wife﴾ i.e., do not divorce her. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ i.e., be mindful of Him regarding her affair, for divorce disgraces her and may injure her heart; and observe the right of Allah concerning yourself as well, for perhaps you will not find after her anything better than her. She had been arrogant toward him because of her nobility, and she would harm him with her tongue, so he intended to divorce her, citing her arrogance and her harm. **The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[40] ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any of your men﴾: This is a rebuttal of a reproach made out of ignorance, when someone said, "Muhammad married the wife of his son Zayd." Allah, Exalted is He, refuted this by saying that it could only be conceived if he, ﷺ, were truly the father of Zayd. But he was not the father of any of his companions, such that there would hold between him and them what holds between a father and his son of the prohibition of in-law marriage and of marriage. Zayd was one of those who were not, in reality, his sons, so his ruling was their ruling. Adoption (al-tabanni) and claiming a child as one's own (al-idda') are only a matter of special favour and closeness. ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah﴾: that is, he was the Messenger of Allah, conveying His messages. ﴿And the Seal of the Prophets﴾: it is read with a fatha and with a kasra on the letter *ta'*, both being two recitations. That is, this is his description and this is his attribute, so he is not in the position of a biological father. Prophethood was sealed with him because he was prescribed laws that suit the interests of people in every time and every place, for the Noble Qur'an left no principle among the principles of benefit without making it clear, nor any noble quality among the foundations of virtues without reviving it. Thus the messages were completed by his message to all people, and the truth of this became evident by the failure of everyone who claimed prophethood after him, until Allah inherits the earth and whoever is upon it, and He is the Best of Inheritors. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾: that is, He does not decree except what His knowledge has preceded, His will has taken effect in, and His wisdom has required.

**Two notes on the subtleties and the remarkable benefits of this story:**

**The first:** The reports do not differ that it was revealed concerning the story of Zayd ibn Harithah and his wife Zaynab bint Jahsh. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Anas in the *Tafsir* (chapter), and he narrated it from him in *al-Tawhid* (chapter), saying: "Zayd ibn Harithah came complaining, and the Prophet ﷺ kept saying, 'Fear Allah and keep your wife.'" Ahmad narrated it with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the house of Zayd ibn Harithah. Zayd came to him complaining about her. He said to him, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah.' Then it was revealed."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this story through al-Suddi, and he related it in a good and clear manner, its wording being: "It has reached us that this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh. Her mother was Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib, the paternal aunt of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to marry her to Zayd ibn Harithah, his freedman, but she disliked that. Then she was pleased with what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had done, and he married her to him. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed His Prophet ﷺ afterwards that she would be among his wives. He was shy to order him to divorce her, and there continued to occur between Zayd and Zaynab what occurs between people. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to keep his wife and to fear Allah. He feared that people would blame him and say, 'He married his son's wife,' for he had adopted Zayd."

And with him, and through the chain of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali, he said: "Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ that Zaynab would be among his wives before he married her. When Zayd came to him complaining about her and said to him, 'Fear Allah and keep your wife,' Allah said: (I have informed you that I will marry her to you), ﴿and you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]."

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*, after quoting what has preceded: "Other reports have come which Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabari narrated, and which many exegetes transmitted, but it is not fitting to occupy oneself with them, and what I have cited from them is the reliable one." End of quote.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir mentioned here reports which we prefer to pass over in silence, because they are not authentic, so we will not cite them." End of quote.

**The second:** Qadi Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said in *al-Shifa*, in discussing the worldly statements of the Prophet ﷺ: "It is not permissible for him ﷺ to order someone to do something or forbid someone from something while he inwardly holds the opposite. He, peace be upon him, has said: 'It is not for a prophet to have the treachery of the eyes; so how could he have the treachery of the heart?'" If you say: what then is the meaning of His saying in the story of Zayd: ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], etc.? Know, may Allah honour you, and do not doubt in the exoneration of the Prophet, peace be upon him, from this apparent meaning, namely that he ordered Zayd to keep her while he loved his divorcing her. This was reported from a group of exegetes, but the most authentic of what is related in this matter is what the people of exegesis have transmitted from Ali ibn Husayn: that Allah, Exalted is He, had informed His Prophet that Zaynab would be among his wives. When Zayd complained about her to him, the Prophet ﷺ said to him, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah,' and he concealed within himself what Allah had informed him, that he would marry her, which Allah was to disclose and manifest by the full completion of the marriage and Zayd's divorce of her." 

Al-Zuhri narrated something similar through Amr ibn Fa'id, who said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, descended upon the Prophet ﷺ to inform him that Allah was marrying him to Zaynab bint Jahsh. That is what he concealed within himself." This is confirmed by the exegetes' statement regarding His words after this: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], meaning: you must marry her. And this is clarified by the fact that Allah, Exalted is He, did not disclose from His command concerning her anything other than his marriage to her, which shows that it is what he, peace be upon him, had concealed, of what Allah, Exalted is He, had informed him of. And His saying, Exalted is He, in the story: ﴿There is no restriction upon the Prophet concerning that which Allah has ordained for him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 38] indicates that there was no restriction upon him in the matter. Had it been as is said, that she had fallen into his heart and that he loved Zayd's divorcing her, there would have been the greatest restriction upon him. How can it be said that he saw her and she pleased him, when she was the daughter of his paternal aunt, and he had been seeing her since she was born, and women did not veil from him, peace be upon him, while she was the wife of Zayd? Rather, Allah made Zayd's divorce of her and the Prophet ﷺ's marriage to her in order to remove the sanctity of adoption and to nullify its cause, as He said: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any of your men﴾, and He said: ﴿So that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]. Ibn Fawrak said: "The meaning of *khashyah* (fear) here is not dread, but rather *istihya'* (shyness); that is, he was shy before them lest they say, 'He married his son's wife.' His fear, peace be upon him, of people was of the agitation of the hypocrites and the Jews and their stirring up of trouble among the Muslims by saying, 'He married his son's wife after forbidding marriage to the wives of sons,' as they used to say. So Allah, Exalted is He, reproached him for this, or cleansed him from turning towards them in what He had made lawful for him, just as He reproached him for seeking the pleasure of his wives in Surah al-Tahrim with His saying: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1], etc. Likewise His saying here." End of his summarized quote.

**The third:** Imam Ibn Hazm said in *al-Fasl*, refuting those who used verses like this one as evidence for the permissibility of minor sins from the prophets: "As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], etc., we have already dealt with this, for there was in it no disobedience at all, nor any opposition to what Allah, Exalted is He, had commanded him. What he had intended was marriage, which is permissible for him to do, permissible for him to leave, permissible for him to keep private, and permissible for him to reveal. The Prophet ﷺ only feared people in this matter, lest they say and suppose a supposition and thereby perish, as he, peace be upon him, said to the two Ansari men: 'It is Safiyyah'; they were amazed at that, so the Prophet ﷺ informed them that 'he only feared that Satan would cast something into their hearts.'" What he, peace be upon him, feared for people, namely the ruin of their religion through a suspicion they might hold about him, peace be upon him, is precisely what these forsaken opponents of ours in this field realise. The will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was that He would disclose what was in his soul, because of the happiness that had preceded in His knowledge for our mother Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her." End of quote.

**The fourth:** The Mufti of Egypt, may Allah have mercy on him, has a statement on this verse. I have seen fit to quote it here to reinforce what has preceded, and as a pause amid the secrets of the verse, to savour what has been described. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was the daughter of his paternal aunt, -ﷺ- Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib. The Messenger proposed her for his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah, but she refused and her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh refused. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36], etc. When the verse was revealed, they both said: 'We are pleased, O Messenger of Allah.' So he married her to him." He also related that he gave her as her dowry sixty dirhams, a headscarf, a wrapper, a shirt, a garment, fifty *mudd* of food, and thirty *sa'* of dates. Thus it is narrated.

On the one hand, we see that Zaynab was the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ's paternal aunt, raised under his watch, and his care encompassed her as it encompasses a daughter with her father from the very beginning, to the extent that he chose her as a wife for his freedman, despite her refusal and her brother's refusal, and he counted their refusal as disobedience. And it remained so until a Qur'an was revealed concerning her. It was as if he compelled her to marry him, because of the benefit Allah inspired him to see for her and for the Muslims in that. Had beauty had any power over his heart, peace be upon him, the strongest power it would have had over him would have been the beauty of a virgin in her youthful bloom and the freshness of her youth. He used to see her, with no veil between him and her, and nothing of her apparent beauty was hidden from him. Yet he did not desire her for himself; he encouraged her towards his freedman. How then could his gaze extend to her, and the arrow of her love strike his heart, after she had become the wife of one of his servants whom he had blessed with manumission and freedom? In what generally prevails among human nature, it is not known that the desire of a relative and his infatuation with a relative should grow so great as to reach the limit of passion, especially if she had been his companion since childhood. Rather, what is customary is the indifference of relatives towards one another, once they have become accustomed to looking at one another from the beginning of their age until it reaches a point where the gaze of desire roams. So how could one think or imagine that the Prophet, to whom Allah says: ﴿And do not extend your eyes towards that which We have given to some pairs of them as the splendour of worldly life﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131], would oppose the customary practice, and then oppose the command of Allah in that? Or how can it come to mind that one whom Allah has protected from every base thing, passion would overpower him for the daughter of his paternal aunt, after he himself had married her to a servant of his?

On the other hand, you see that the Prophet ﷺ, who was compassionate and merciful, did not mind Zaynab's refusal and her aversion to Zayd. He well knew that the aversion of a woman's heart from her husband is something by which living together becomes miserable and the affairs of life are corrupted. It was not for him, the master of reformers, to compel a woman to be joined with a man whom she does not desire, given the clear harm this entails for each of the two spouses.

There is no doubt that we find in this a guide to the correct understanding of the verse we are currently explaining. For the attachment of adopted children to households and their association with their lineages was something the Arabs held to, and regarded as a foundation to which they returned in matters of honour and lineage. They would give the adopted child all the rights of a son, and apply to him and against him all the rulings they considered applicable to a son, even in inheritance and the sanctity of lineage. This was a wretched pre-Islamic belief, which Allah willed to erase with Islam, so that only the clear lineage would be recognised, and only those rulings with a sound basis would be applied. For this reason Allah revealed: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying with your mouths, but Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4]. Then He said: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5], etc. This is the divine justice: that no one obtains the right of a son unless he is a son.

As for the adopted son (al-mutabanna) and the one attached by claim (al-lasiq), he has no right except the right of a mawla (client or freed slave) and a brother in faith. Thus God forbade the Muslims to attribute the adoptee (al-da'i) to the one who adopted him, and He prohibited them from taking from the son's rights anything for him, be it little or much. He made the matter so severe that He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but [only for] what your hearts have intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5]. So He pardons the utterance that proceeds without intent, such as when a man says to another, "This is my son," or when someone is called by such a term without intending adoption. But He does not pardon the deliberate act of that, which is intended to attach him to that lineage, as was known before. The sunnah (established way) of God in His creation has passed: that what has taken root in the soul by force of custom is not easily freed from. None can do so except one whom God raises above customs, frees from the bondage of desires, and makes his resolve higher than what is familiar. Such a person is not swayed, that is, not inclined, except by the truth; habit does not rule him, and custom does not overcome him. That is the Prophet ﷺ, and whoever God singles out to follow him. For this reason, whenever God forbade something disliked, while the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance) was upon it, or permitted something that the Jahiliyyah had prohibited, the Prophet ﷺ hastened to comply with the prohibition by abstaining from what was forbidden and doing its opposite, and he hastened to carry out the command by performing what was commanded, so that he would be a good example and a righteous model that souls imitate and resolves follow, and so that the burden of custom would lighten and minds would be freed from the doubt of uncertainty. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proclaimed at the Farewell Pilgrimage the prohibition of usury (riba), and the first usury he abolished was the usury of his paternal uncle al-Abbas, so that people would see his practice with the nearest of people to him and the most honoured by him, and it would become easy for them to leave their wealth, and the whisperings of Satan would be cut off from their breasts.

Upon this divine sunnah the Prophet ﷺ acted in the matter of Zaynab. It was hard for the Arabs to separate from their families those whom they had attached to their lineages as adoptees, as indicated by His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], etc. So the Prophet ﷺ, following His sunnah, purposely broke the custom himself, though it was not fitting for him, nor consistent with wisdom, to order one of the distant adoptees to marry, then order him to divorce, then order the one who had adopted him to marry his divorced wife. For in that there is hardship, given the dominance of custom and the entrenched aversion in souls, which is no secret to anyone. So God inspired him to undertake the matter himself with one of his freedmen, so that the custom would fall in deed, just as He had annulled its ruling by decisive word. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ compelled Zaynab to marry Zayd, who was his mawla, and the Prophet found in himself that this marriage was a prelude to establishing a legal ruling and implementing a divine command.

After Zaynab went to Zayd, her initial aversion did not soften and her leadership did not become submissive. Rather, she held her nose high, and began to harm her husband and boast over him with her lineage, and with her being nobler than him in origin and purer than him in freedom, because she had never been subjected to slavery as he had been. So he complained of her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ time and again. He, peace be upon him, despite his lofty station, was overcome by modesty, so he delayed and tarried in carrying out the command of God and did not hasten. So he would say to Zayd: "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah." Until the command of God prevailed over the matter of pride, and He permitted Zayd to divorce her after living with her had pained him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her afterwards, in order to tear the veil of that custom and break that door which had been closed against opposing it, as He said: ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need of them; and ever is the command of Allah accomplished﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]. He confirmed this by explicitly negating doubt in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], the verse. This is the sound narration and the preponderant opinion.

Then he said: As for what they narrated, that "the Prophet passed by the house of Zayd while he was absent, and saw Zaynab, and something of her fell into his heart, so he said: 'Glory be to the Turner of hearts!' She heard the glorification and conveyed it to Zayd, and it occurred to him to divorce her," etc., which they related, Imam Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said it is not authentic. Those who transmit it and argue with it to support their claims regarding the interpretation of the verse have not appreciated the station of prophethood as it deserves, and their minds did not grasp the reality of infallibility (ismah). He elaborated on this, and I will mention from his words what supports our mention concerning these narrations.

He said, after discussing the infallibility of the Prophet ﷺ and his purity from defect in the time of Jahiliyyah, and after Islam had come: "We have already presented to you narrations all of whose chains are invalid. The authentic among them is what is reported from Aisha, that she said: 'If the Prophet ﷺ had concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], meaning with Islam, ﴿and you bestowed favour upon him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], by freeing him: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], to His saying: ﴿and was the command of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].' And when the Messenger of Allah married her, they said: 'He has married the wife of his son,' so Allah revealed: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, the verse."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had adopted him when he was young, and he remained until he became a man, and he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad. So Allah revealed: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5], meaning that it is more just in the sight of Allah. The judge (al-Qadi) said: "What lies beyond this verse is not to be considered. As for their saying that the Prophet ﷺ saw her and she fell into his heart, it is false. For he was with her at every time and place, and there was no veil at that time, so how could [desire] arise in him toward her and she arise in him, and he look at her every hour, yet she not fall into his heart, unless she had a husband? And she had given herself to him and disliked anyone else, so it did not occur to his mind. How then could a desire arise that had not been! Far be that pure heart from this corrupt attachment. And He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have provided [enjoyment] to categories of them, the flower of the worldly life, that We may test them therein﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131]. Women are the most seductive of flowers and the most fragrant of herbs. If this applies to the divorced, how then to the married who are confined?"

Then he proceeded with the discussion of the verse itself according to what is authentically established about the incident. Had it not been for fear of lengthening, I would have transcribed his words verbatim. Glory be to Allah! How could Muslim people accept belief in such narrations, when they know that Allah did not leave His Prophet to turn away from Ibn Umm Maktum and to pursue the chieftains of Quraysh in hope of their conversion, until He rebuked him for that in His saying: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ [Abasa: 1], and the verses to the end, even though he did not turn away from the blind man except because he was occupied with what he considered in himself to be good for the religion, and not out of desire for status, nor greed for wealth, (p-4875) nor ambition for pleasure.

So if the narration they claim concerning Zaynab were sound, the reproach would be for that utterance in Zaynab's hearing, and then for the marriage after divorce, as He indicated in the story of Dawud, peace be upon him. But Muhammad ﷺ, in the height of his station and the elevation of his rank in prophethood, would not have his soul aspire to delight in the daughter of his paternal aunt and the wife of his mawla, nor would he let her hear what indicates his passion for her, nor let his resolve weaken in suppressing his desire and restraining its excess. The Lord of Muhammad would not justify his desire or indulge his whim in what contradicts His command, He who forbade him to extend his eyes toward what He gave people to enjoy of the flower of the worldly life, and among its flowers are women. The rank of Muhammad is exalted above that, and the station of his Lord is exalted far above this.

By God! Were it not for what the weak or the deceitful introduced of such narrations, nothing of what they aim at would have occurred to anyone who considers the noble verse. For the text of the verse is apparent and clear, and its meaning does not admit interpretation, and it does not come to the mind from it except that the reproach was for haste in the matter and deliberation about it, and that what he was concealing in himself was that divine command issued to him, that he should demolish that custom rooted in the souls of the Arabs, and that he himself should take up the pickaxe to demolish it, just as it was decreed for him to break their idols with his own hand for the first time at the conquest of Makkah, and as is his way in everything he forbade of their customs. What he was concealing in himself, Allah would manifest through His command which He revealed to him in His Book, and through his marriage to the wife of the one they used to call his son, as its explanation has preceded. Nothing prevented him from manifesting what Allah had manifested except the modesty of the noble and the deliberateness of the wise, with the knowledge that he would certainly act, but together with the assistance of time."

Then the Imam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I will mention a subtle point of some intelligent people that occurred in my presence before one of the American professors. Mention came of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿who perfected everything He created﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7]. The American said: "Even Zaynab, the wife of Zayd ibn Harithah," alluding by this saying to that incident and insinuating his love for Zaynab, as they claimed. My companion said to him: "Glory be to Allah! You occupy yourselves with the sciences of the heavens (p-4876) and the earth, and do not use your minds on the closest things to you, though you are, as is well known of you, among the most eager of people to investigate religions. Indeed Allah commanded His Prophet to marry the wife of the one who called him his son, so as to show people in practice that not everyone who is given the title of son is truly a son. If Christ was called 'the Son' in the language of the Gospel, this is not in the literal sense; rather, the true 'son' is one who is born of his father by a valid birth. Surely in that is a reminder for the worlds." And Allah knows best. End of his words, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him.

Fifth: Imam Ahmad, Muslim and al-Nasa'i related from Anas, who said: "When the 'idda (waiting period) of Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd ibn Harithah: 'Go and mention her to me.' So he set off until he came to her, and she was kneading her dough. He said: 'When I saw her, she became great in my breast, until I could not look at her, and I said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and retreated backwards, and I said: O Zaynab! Rejoice. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to mention you. She said: I will do nothing until I consult my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. So she stood up to her place of worship, and the Qur'an was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered upon her without permission. And indeed we saw, when she entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, he fed us bread and meat over her [wedding feast]."

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: This too is among the most eloquent of what occurred in that matter: that the one who had been her husband was the one who proposed, so that no one would suppose that it happened by compulsion without his consent. In it also is the testing of what he had of her feelings: whether any of it remained or not. In it also is the recommendation that the woman perform istikharah (prayer for guidance) and supplicate at the time of the proposal before responding, and that whoever entrusts his affair to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah will facilitate for him what is best and most beneficial for him in this world and the Hereafter. End of quote. That is: Allah preserved her honour from being lost after her marriage to a mawla. So He chose for her what ennobled her and elevated her station, out of His care and mercy for the Ummah as well.

Sixth: Ibn Jarir related from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Indeed I take pride over you in three things, of which none of your wives takes pride: my grandfather and yours is one; Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, married me to you from the heaven; and the emissary is indeed Jibril, peace be upon him.'"

Al-Bukhari transmitted part of this from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Zaynab used to boast over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Your families married you off, but Allah the Exalted married me to him from above the seven heavens." Ibn al-Qayyim said in (Zad al-Ma'ad): Among the distinctive features of Zaynab is that Allah, glory be to Him, was himself her guardian (wali), who gave her in marriage to His Messenger from above His heavens, and she died at the beginning of the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab. End of quote.

She was first married to Zayd ibn Harithah, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had adopted (tabanna, adoption). When he divorced her, Allah married her to him so that his ummah would follow his example in marrying the wives of those whom they had adopted. End of quote.

Seventh: They said: The general wording of the Exalted's statement ﴿from among your men﴾ is not restricted by the fact that he ﷺ was a father to al-Tahir, al-Qasim and Ibrahim, because they did not reach puberty; and had they reached it, they would have been men belonging to him, ﷺ, not men belonging to themselves. End of quote.

This is an excessive subtlety in analysis; otherwise, the indication of the context is clearer than any restriction of the attribution.

Ibn Kathir said: No male child of his, peace and blessings be upon him, survived to reach puberty. He ﷺ had sons by Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib and al-Tahir, and they all died young. He ﷺ also had a son, Ibrahim, by Mariyah the Copt, who likewise died while still nursing. He ﷺ had four daughters by Khadijah: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with them all. Three of them died during his lifetime, and Fatimah died six months after him. End of quote.

(p-4878) Then Allah the Exalted commanded frequent remembrance of Him and attentiveness to giving thanks for what He had bestowed upon them of guidance to the light of His law, until one forgets the shame of disbelief and its ignorance, through His saying, glory be to Him:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[41–42] "O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance" (Qur'an 33:41). "And exalt Him morning and afternoon" (Qur'an 33:42).

"O you who have believed, remember Allah" (Qur'an 33:41), that is, with what is worthy of Him of the various kinds of praise and glorification. "With much remembrance" (Qur'an 33:41), that is, one that encompasses all times and all states. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Allah the Exalted has not imposed on His servants any obligation without setting for it a known limit, and then excused those who are obliged in cases of necessity, except for remembrance (dhikr), for Allah the Exalted has not set for it any limit at which it ends, and He has excused no one from abandoning it except one whose reason has been overcome, and He has commanded it in all states. So He, the Exalted, said: "Remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on your sides" (Qur'an 4:103), and He said: "Remember Allah with much remembrance" (Qur'an 33:41), that is, by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and while at home, in wealth and in poverty, in sickness and in health, in secret and in public, and in every state.

"And exalt Him morning and afternoon" (Qur'an 33:42), that is, at the beginning of the day and at its end, so that the effect of the glorification (tasbih) may persist in them for the rest of the day and the night; for His remembrance and His glorification bring about the illumination of hearts at the time when they are free from preoccupations.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Glorification (tasbih) is part of remembrance (dhikr), and it was singled out from among its kinds in the same way that Jibril and Mika'il were singled out from among the angels, to show its excellence over the rest of the remembrances. For its meaning is the declaration of the transcendence of His Essence above what is impermissible of attributes and acts. An example of its excellence over other remembrances is the excellence of a servant's describing himself as pure from the filth of sins and cleansed from the impurities of wrongdoing, over his other attributes, such as much prayer and fasting and devotion to all acts of obedience. It is also possible that by remembrance and its abundance is meant the multiplication of acts of obedience and devotion to acts of worship, for every act of obedience and every good is part of remembrance. Then He specified from that glorification "morning and afternoon" (Qur'an 33:42), which is the prayer at all its times, due to the excellence of prayer over other things, or the dawn prayer and the two evening prayers, because performing them is more difficult and observing them is more stringent. And His words, Exalted is He:

And His words, Exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [do likewise], that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He merciful to the believers.﴾

﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [do likewise]﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) serving as a causal explanation (ta'lil) for what precedes it, of the two matters. God's sending blessings upon them, despite their not deserving them and His being free of need from all the worlds, necessitates that they reciprocate by remembering Him and glorifying Him, as is due to Him from them. This is what Abu al-Su'ud conveyed.

Ibn Kathir said: This is an incitement to remembrance, meaning: He, glory be to Him, remembers you, so remember Him yourselves. This is like His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from among you, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151] ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152]. End of quotation.

The word ṣalāh (blessing, prayer) means mercy and compassion. The meaning is: He is the One who shows mercy to you and is tender toward you, in that He calls you to goodness, commands you to frequent remembrance, and to devotion to prayer and obedience. ﴿That He may bring you out from darknesses﴾, meaning the darkness of disbelief, sins, doubts, and bad habits; ﴿into the light﴾, meaning the light of faith, the Sunnah, obedience, and good character. ﴿And ever is He merciful to the believers﴾, meaning: He did not leave them stumbling in the blindness of error and ignorance, but lit the paths for them and made the landmarks clear to them. He mentioned the angels to honor their status and the status of the believers, and to show that the Exalted Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la) has care, compassion, and mercy, through seeking forgiveness, supplication, and praise for what is good, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire."﴾ [Ghafir: 7] ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers and their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ [Ghafir: 8] ﴿And protect them from evil deeds.﴾ [Ghafir: 9] [the verse].

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[47–49] ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.﴾ ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48] ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period [ʿiddah] that you should count. So provide for them and release them in a fair release.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49]

﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾: that is, a great reward and an abundant recompense.

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48]: that is, in what they urge you toward and what they censure of the ways of their ignorance and their customs, by being gentle in conveying the message, being lenient in warning, and being patient in proclaiming the truth.

﴿And disregard their harm﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48]: that is, do not inflict harm upon them in retaliation for their deeds. Rather, pardon and overlook. Or its meaning is: disregard what they harm you with because of your proclaiming the truth to them. Thus the verbal noun (al-maṣdar) is in the genitive construction with its agent according to the first reading, and with its object according to the second.

﴿And rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48]: that is, one to whom affairs are entrusted, and a guarantor of what He has promised you of victory and of the overthrow of those who are disbelievers.

﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49]: that is, when you marry them.
