Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verse 50:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[50] ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whose due compensation you have given, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you as spoils, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, apart from the believers. We have certainly known what We have imposed upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty for you. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whose due compensation you have given﴾ That is, their dowries (mahr), for they are the compensation for intimacy (ujur al-abda'). Their giving (itha') is either handing them over promptly, or naming them in the marriage contract. Prompt payment was the custom and practice of the predecessors (al-salaf), and nothing else was known among them.

Ibn Kathir said: The Prophet ﷺ had for his wives twelve ounces and a nash, which is half an ounce, so the total was five hundred dirhams. Except Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, for whom al-Najashi, may Allah have mercy on him, paid the dowry on his behalf, four hundred dinars. And except Safiyyah bint Huyayy, whom he chose from the captives of Khaybar, then he freed her and made her freedom her dowry. (p-4885) Likewise Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, whose contract of manumission he paid to Thabit ibn Qays, and then he married her, may Allah be pleased with them all. End of quote.

The restriction of the lawfulness for him, upon him be prayer and peace, to the giving of dowries is not because the permissibility depends on it, since a marriage is valid without naming a dowry. Rather, a dowry of equivalent value (mahr al-mithl) or a provision (mut'ah) is obligatory whether or not intercourse occurred. Rather, it is for preferring what is more excellent and better for him, upon him be prayer and peace, like the restriction of the lawfulness of a slave woman to her being a captive, in His saying: ﴿and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you as spoils﴾, for the beginning of the matter of a purchased woman and what befell her is not established.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, He permitted you concessions (tasarri) from what you took from the spoils. He possessed Safiyyah and Juwayriyah, then he freed them and married them, and he possessed Rayhanah bint Shamʿun al-Nadriyyah and Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah, mother of his son Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and both were among the concubines, may Allah be pleased with them both. ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾, that is, from Makkah to Madinah. The restriction is to show what is more excellent, as has preceded. And for them there are several views concerning the singular of the paternal uncle and maternal uncle and the plural of the paternal aunt and maternal aunt; some are subtle and some weak. In my view, the singular and plural follow what the composition requires, the arrangement, the delicacy of expression, and the grace of delivery, as one who tastes the flavour of eloquent speech and drinks from the spring of its fluency knows. Thus the singular in these two places here is more tender and sweeter than the plural, just as in the verse ﴿the houses of your paternal uncles or the houses of your paternal aunts﴾ [al-Nur: 61] the plural is firmer and more eloquent than the singular. For every situation there is a fitting speech, and for every field a fitting state. ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾, that is, marries her and is inclined to accept her gift of herself without a dowry. He named among the women who gave themselves: Maymunah bint al-Harith, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah Umm al-Masakin al-Ansariyyah, Umm Sharik bint Jabir, and Khawlah bint Hakim, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(p-4886) In al-Bukhari, from ʿAʾishah, she said: "I used to feel jealous of those who gave themselves to the Prophet ﷺ, and I would say: Does a woman give herself? But when Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿You may put off whom you wish of them and take to yourself whom you wish﴾ [al-Ahzab: 51], up to the verse, I said: I see that your Lord only hastens to your desire."

And from Ibn ʿAbbas, that there was not with him ﷺ any woman who gave herself to him; that is, he did not accept that, although it was permissible for him, because it is subject to his will. And Allah knows best.

Ibn al-Qayyim said: As for those whom he ﷺ proposed to and did not marry, and those who gave themselves to him and he did not marry, they are about four or five. Some said they are thirty women. But the people of knowledge of the biography and the circumstances of the Prophet ﷺ do not know this; rather, they deny it.

Abu al-Suʿud said: His mention, upon him be prayer and peace, in both places by the title of prophethood, by way of iltifat (shift of address), is for honour and to indicate that it is the basis for the establishment of the ruling, so it is specific to him, peace be upon him, in accordance with its specificity to him, as is conveyed by His saying: ﴿exclusively for you﴾, that is, the lawfulness of her has been made purely for you, exclusively, meaning by purity; so it is a emphatic verbal noun (masdar), or its adjective, that is, a gift that is exclusive: ﴿apart from the believers﴾, that is, the woman who gives herself is not lawful for them except with a guardian and a dowry, lest women take concubines and immorality spread under the pretext of that. Qatadah said: There is no woman who gives herself to a man without a guardian or a dowry except for the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿We have certainly known what We have imposed upon them﴾, that is, upon the believers: ﴿concerning their wives﴾, that is, concerning their lawfulness, from the guardian, the witnesses and the named dowry: ﴿and those whom their right hands possess﴾, that is, concerning their lawfulness, regarding the widening of the matter in it.

Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: It was interpreted as istibra' (waiting period to ensure a womb is clear), and it is not mentioned in the Qur'an except here.

﴿so that there will be no difficulty for you﴾, that is, narrowness. The lam is connected to ﴿exclusively﴾, or to a verb understood from what precedes (p-4887), that is: We have certainly known what We imposed upon them, and We removed it from you to lift the difficulty and constraint from you, in what wisdom and care for you required. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, He forgives what is hard to guard against, and shows mercy by widening where there would be difficulty.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[51] ﴿You may defer whom you will of them, and take to you whom you will. And whomever you desire of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they all be pleased with what you give them. Allah knows what is in your hearts, and ever is Allah Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

﴿تُرْجِي﴾ (turji) is read with a hamza and without a hamza. It means: you leave aside and postpone. ﴿Whom you will of them﴾ means: of these women whom We have made lawful to you, so that you do not marry them. ﴿And take to you whom you will﴾ means: you take into your marriage whomever of them you will. ﴿And whomever you desire of those you had set aside﴾ means: whomever you choose to marry after postponing her. ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ means: in taking her to yourself.

Some of them held the view that the pronoun in ﴿مِنهُنَّ﴾ (minhunna, "of them") refers to the women who gave themselves away (al-wahibat). Al-Sha'bi said: "They were women who gave themselves to the Prophet (ﷺ). He consummated with some of them and postponed others, and none of them were married after him, among them Umm Sharik." It is supported by the hadith of Aisha in Ahmad's collection, that "she used to rebuke the women who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: 'Is a woman not ashamed to offer herself without a dowry?' When Allah revealed ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾ to the end of the verse, she said: 'I see that your Lord hastens to fulfil your desire.'" Al-Bukhari also narrated it, as has already been mentioned.

Others held that the meaning of the verse is: you divorce whom you will of your wives and release them, and you keep whom you will of them and do not divorce. It is also reported from Qatada that it concerns the division of nights (al-qasam, the rotation of nights among wives), that he may divide for whom he wishes and leave it for whom he wishes. Yet the Prophet (ﷺ) never left off dividing. Whoever held that the division was not obligatory upon him (ﷺ) argued from this verse. The verification is that the verse is general (al-'amm) in all of that, and that what has been transmitted of what was mentioned is by way of being content with some individual instances of the general, or from an opinion its proponent held.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That﴾ means: what has been mentioned of leaving the matter to your will and lifting the burden of blame from you in it. ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾ means: their souls are content, if they know that this is from Allah, exalted is He. ﴿And they not grieve﴾ at the violation of postponement. ﴿And that they all be pleased with what you give them﴾ means: because it is a ruling in which they are all equal. If you equalize among them, they will take that as preference; otherwise they know it is by the ruling of Allah, exalted is He, so their souls are reassured by it. ﴿Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ means: of the inclination towards some of them over others in love. ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing﴾ means: of the secrets of the breasts. ﴿Forbearing﴾ means: possessor of forbearance towards His servants, so He pardons and forgives.

Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan (ahl al-sunan) narrated from Aisha that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to divide among his wives and be just. Then he would say: 'O Allah, this is my action in what I control, so do not blame me in what You control and I do not.'" He meant the heart.

[p-4888]

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verse 52:**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[52] ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever Watchful over all things.﴾

﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this﴾, i.e., after the women whose lawfulness for you was stated in the preceding verse. Consider how Allah, exalted is He, honoured His Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, by not saying to him: "And what is beyond that is forbidden to you." He addressed the believers with a similar expression, so that you may know how people differ in their rank through the manner of address, as they differ in the lofty degrees.

I have not seen anyone draw attention to this, so take care to attend to it in this verse and in similar ones.

Mujahid said regarding the verse: that is, it is not lawful for you [to take] a Jewish woman, a Christian woman, or any disbelieving woman. ﴿Nor to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses﴾, that is, you may have concubinage with them, even if they are People of the Book or polytheists, because they do not have the rights of free women. ﴿And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾, that is, [He is Watchful] in that He made lawful what He made lawful and prohibited what He prohibited for the Prophet and for the community, through an exposition that leaves no obscurity, and with a wisdom that admits no injustice.

Some exegetes (mufassirun) have held that the meaning of the verse is the prohibition of marrying anyone beyond the nine wives he had, ﷺ, and that nine is his limit just as four is the limit for others, and that this was a recompense for their choosing him when he gave them the choice, as has preceded in the verse. Then they said that Allah, exalted is He, lifted the burden from him in this matter, abrogated (naskh) the ruling of this verse, and permitted him to marry, but he did not do so, in completion of the favour upon them. Others among them said that it is definitive (muhkamah) and not abrogated. All of that has no proof behind it, is a dismantling of the meaning, and is heedlessness of the secret of His honouring him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, through the intended purpose of the address. Ziyad, a man of the Ansar, erred in this meaning, and Ubayy, may Allah be pleased with him, turned him back to the correct meaning. This is what was narrated by Abdullah ibn Ahmad and Ibn Jarir: that Ziyad said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet ﷺ died, would it not have been lawful for him to marry?" He said: "What would prevent him from that?" He said: "His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this﴾." Ubayy said to him: "Allah only made lawful for him a type of women." Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50] — up to His words — ﴿if a woman gives herself to the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50]. Then it was said to him: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this﴾.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade kinds of women except those who were believing emigrants, by His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this﴾, the verse." So he prohibited every woman of a religion other than Islam.

Whoever looks at what they wrote here will be struck with wonder at how far they have strayed from its purpose. Praise belongs to Allah for the inspiration of truth and its teaching.

**Note:**

The author of (Lubab al-Ta'wil) said: In His words, ﴿even though their beauty pleases you﴾, there is evidence for the permissibility of looking at the woman a man intends to marry. This is supported by what was narrated from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If one of you proposes to a woman, and he is able to look at what will move him to marry her, let him do so." Abu Dawud recorded it.

Muslim narrated from Abu Hurairah that a man wanted to marry a woman from the Ansar. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the Ansar." Al-Humaydi said: "He means smallness (al-sighar)."

And from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: "I proposed to a woman. The Prophet ﷺ said to me: 'Did you look at her?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Look at her, for it is more likely to create affection between you two.'" Al-Tirmidhi recorded it and graded it as good (hasan).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 33, verse 53:

(p-4891) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[53] ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given you for a meal, without awaiting its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that would cause offense to the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask of them [the wives of the Prophet] something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not [permissible] for you to offend the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormity.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given you for a meal, without awaiting its preparation﴾ This is an address to some of the Companions, and it forbids them from entering his ﷺ dwellings without permission, as they used to do in their houses in the Jahiliyyah and at the beginning of Islam. The phrase "ila" (for/to) is connected to "yu'dhana" (permission is given) by implying the meaning of invitation, to indicate that they should not enter upon food without an invitation, even if permission has been established; as His saying indicates: ﴿without awaiting its preparation﴾, i.e., not waiting for its time and its readiness.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, do not watch the food when it is cooked, so that when it nears completion you position yourselves to enter, for this is something Allah dislikes and censures. This is evidence for the prohibition of tatful (uninvited hanging about at a meal), which the Arabs call al-dayfan (the parasite guest). Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi wrote a book on this subject, condemning the tufayliyyin (uninvited diners), and mentioned from their reports things whose citation would be lengthy. End of quote.

I say: The meaning of His words ﴿without awaiting its preparation﴾ may be a prohibition for them from entering, even though they are permitted and invited, before the appointed time set for their attendance, out of haste and waiting for the food to ripen. (p-4892) For that is something that hurts the heart of the host, since it occupies this portion of time with them without benefit, except the constriction of the host's chest and his household, the occupation of his time, the generation of idle talk, the forced speech that is unnecessary, and the prolonging of the period of veiling for his wives. This is nothing but the ill-omen of hastening before the time. For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But when you are invited, then enter﴾, i.e., when you are invited to enter at its time, then enter at it, not before it nor after it. So "lakin" (but) is an exception from the prohibition of entering, together with the unrestricted permission which is the invitation, by teaching another manners and conveying an important condition: namely, an indication that the invitation has a time and a moment whose timing must be observed. This prohibited behaviour is still committed by the heavy-footed among the rustics and those like them among the coarse townspeople, who have not been disciplined by the manners of the Noble Book and the purified Sunnah; that is, when they are invited to partake of food, they hasten to arrive hours before its time, which distresses the soul of the host and his household, and wastes for them a precious portion of their time in vain, except for listening to their insipid talk and their unwelcome service, as we have mentioned. Accordingly, on what we have mentioned, the verse contains a beautiful benefit and an important ruling, namely the prohibition of coming before the appointed time. In that case the word (ghayra, "without awaiting") is a second circumstantial clause of the subject, restricting the permitted entering to being at the time of the invitation, not before it. The implied sense is: "unless you are permitted, being in the state of not awaiting its preparation." Hence it has been said: it is the verse of the heavy-footed. Having known this, the more appropriate course is to derive the prohibition of tatful from the beginning of the verse, which is: ﴿do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given you﴾, and from His saying: ﴿But when you are invited, then enter﴾, not from His saying: ﴿without awaiting its preparation﴾, because that has a particular meaning, which is what we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

Benefit:

(al-Ini): is a verbal noun. It is said: anā al-shay'a ya'nā ani'an with a fatha (anā, with a fatha, shortened). And (ana): with fatha and shortened, and (ini): with kasra and shortened, meaning: it has come due and arrived. 'Amr ibn Hassan said:

It is the fate that has been in labour for him on a day when it has come due, and for every pregnant woman there is completion.

Then He, glorified be He, pointed to another manner with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when you have eaten, disperse﴾, i.e., scatter and do not (p-4893) linger. ﴿Nor remaining for conversation﴾, i.e., for the conversation of some of you with others, or for the conversation of the household by eavesdropping on it. It is conjoined to ("without awaiting"), or it is implicitly governed by a verb; i.e., do not linger seeking familiarity. ﴿Indeed, that﴾, i.e., the thing prohibited in the verse, ﴿would cause offense to the Prophet﴾, i.e., by constricting what is revealed to him and to his household and occupying him with what does not concern him. ﴿And he is shy of [dismissing] you﴾, i.e., from indicating to you that you should disperse. ﴿But Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, meaning that your dispersing is a truth. It should therefore not be abandoned out of shyness, just as Allah does not abandon it out of the shyness of the bashful, so He commanded you to it. The word "truth" is placed in the position of dispersal to magnify its importance. It was read as "la yastahi" with the first ya' omitted and its vowel thrown onto the ha'; ﴿And when you ask of them﴾: the pronoun refers to the wives of the Prophet, indicated by the mention of his houses, peace be upon him; ﴿something﴾, i.e., a thing to be enjoyed; ﴿then ask them from behind a screen﴾, i.e., a curtain; ﴿that﴾, i.e., what has been mentioned of not entering without permission, not seeking familiarity for conversation upon entering, and asking for goods from behind a screen; ﴿is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾, i.e., from satanic thoughts regarding inclination towards them and towards you; meaning that purification from it is obligatory, because of what it contains of harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. For this reason He said: ﴿And it is not [permissible] for you to offend the Messenger of Allah﴾, i.e., to do an act by which he would be harmed during his life; ﴿nor to marry his wives after him﴾, i.e., after his death, not merely until the end of the waiting period, but ﴿ever﴾; ﴿Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾, i.e., a grave matter and a monstrous affair, whose magnitude cannot be measured, because of what it contains of violating the sanctity of His beloved ﷺ.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In it is [a demonstration of] His, the Exalted's, magnifying the status of His Messenger ﷺ and making his sanctity obligatory, alive and dead, which is not hidden; for this reason the Exalted went to great lengths in the warning when He said:

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[54] ﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿Whether you disclose a thing﴾, i.e., of what has no good in it, such as marrying them by your tongues, according to what is narrated from some of the boorish: ﴿or conceal it﴾, i.e., in your souls. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾, i.e., He will certainly recompense you [p-4894] for what proceeds from you of disobedience, whether apparent or hidden. In this generalization, together with the proof for the intended meaning, there is additional intimidation, emphasis, and exaggeration in the warning.

Ibn Kathir said: The scholars are unanimous that whoever was widowed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among his wives, it is forbidden for anyone else to marry her after him, because they are his wives in this world and the Hereafter, and the Mothers of the Believers. They differed concerning one who consummated marriage with her and then divorced her during his lifetime: is it permissible for another to marry her? There are two opinions. The basis of the two is whether she is included in the generality of His saying: ﴿after him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53] or not. As for one who married her and then divorced her before consummation, we know of no dispute, in this situation, regarding her being lawful for another, and Allah knows best. End of quotation.

**Note:**

In al-Iklil: This is the verse of the veil (hijab) which He commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe, after the women had not been veiling. It contains the permissibility of hearing their speech and addressing them, and it contains the prohibition of harming the Prophet ﷺ by all forms of harm. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir also said: This is the verse of the veil. It contains rulings and legal etiquettes, and it is among those matters in which its revelation agreed with the statement of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, as al-Bukhari narrated from him that he said: "O Messenger of Allah! The righteous and the wicked enter upon you. Would that you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe the veil!" So Allah revealed the verse of the veil.

And he (ʿUmar) used to say: "If she obeyed you regarding them, no eye would have seen them."

The time of its revelation was the morning after the wedding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Zaynab bint Jahsh, whose marriage Allah Himself, Exalted is He, undertook. That was in Dhu al-Qaʿdah of the fifth year, according to Qatadah, al-Waqidi, and others. But Abu ʿUbaydah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna and Khalifah ibn Khayyat claimed that it was in the third year. Allah knows best.

[p-4895] Al-Bukhari narrated from Anas, who said: "When the Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people, and they ate, then sat conversing. When he appeared to be preparing to rise, they did not rise. When he saw that, he rose; when he rose, those who were going to rise rose, but three persons remained seated. The Prophet ﷺ came to enter, but the people were seated. Then they rose and left, so I came and informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had left. He came until he entered, and I went to enter, but he placed the curtain between me and him. Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], to the end of the verse."

Muslim and al-Nasai also narrated it.

And from Anas also, he said: "The Prophet ﷺ consummated the marriage with Zaynab bint Jahsh with bread and meat. I was sent to call people to the food, so people would come, eat, and leave; then another group would come, eat, and leave. I called until I could not find anyone to call. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I cannot find anyone to call.' He said: 'Lift up your food.' Three men remained, conversing in the house. The Prophet ﷺ went out and proceeded to the chamber of ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the house, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' She said: 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. How did you find your wife, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah bless you.'

He then went around the chambers of all his wives. He would say to them what he said to ʿAʾishah, and they would say to him what ʿAʾishah said. Then the Prophet ﷺ returned, and behold, three men were in the house conversing — and the Prophet ﷺ was very shy — so he went out heading toward the chamber of ʿAʾishah. I do not know whether she informed him or he was informed that the people had left. So he returned, until when he placed his foot on the threshold of the door, inside, and the other outside, he let the curtain fall between me and him, and the verse of the veil was revealed."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and Muslim and al-Tirmidhi narrated something similar; as Ibn Kathir expounded.

[p-4896] The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: ʿIyad said: The veil was obligatory upon them as a matter specific to them. It was made obligatory upon them without dispute, regarding the face and the two hands, so it is not permissible for them to uncover that in testimony or otherwise, nor to display their persons even if they are covered, except where a necessity calls for it, such as relieving oneself. He then cited what is in al-Muwatta that when ʿUmar died, Hafsah was screened by the women so that her person would not be seen, and that Zaynab bint Jahsh had a canopy placed over her bier so that her person would be concealed. End of quotation.

There is no evidence in what he mentioned for what he claimed, that it was obligatory upon them in that manner. They continued after the Prophet ﷺ to perform the Hajj and circumambulation, and the Companions and those after them would hear hadith from them, while their bodies were covered, though not their persons. And it has already been mentioned in the chapter on Hajj the statement of Ibn Jurayj to ʿAta', when he mentioned to him the circumambulation of ʿAʾishah: "Was it before the veil or after it?" He said: "I encountered that after the veil." End of quotation.

What supports this is what al-Bukhari narrated in the Tafsir from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Sawdah went out after the veil had been imposed, for some need of hers, and she was a large woman, not concealed from one who knew her. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab saw her and said: 'O Sawdah! By Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look at how you go out.' She said: So she turned back, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house, and he was having his evening meal with a bone in his hand. She entered and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! I went out for some need of mine, and ʿUmar said to me such and such.' She said: Then Allah revealed to him, then it was lifted from him, and the bone was still in his hand, which he had not put down. He said: 'Indeed, it has been permitted for you to go out for your needs.'"

Al-Kirmani said: If you say, it occurred here that it was after the veil had been imposed, and in Wudu' (i.e., in al-Bukhari) that it was before the veil, the answer is: perhaps it occurred twice.

[p-4897] Ibn Hajar said: I say, rather, the intended first veil is other than the second veil.

The conclusion is that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, had within his heart an aversion to strangers looking upon the sacred precinct of the Prophet, until he declared to him, upon him be prayers and peace: "Veil your wives." He emphasized that until the verse of the veil was revealed. Then after that he intended that they should not display their persons at all, even if covered, and he exaggerated in that, so he was prevented from it, and they were permitted to go out for their needs, to remove hardship and lift difficulty. End of quotation, verbatim. We have only quoted the reconciliation of the two narrations, although what is more relevant to it is the explanation of the Sahih, because many exegetes have transmitted one of the two narrations and others the second, which may cause the reader to fall into the suspicion of contradiction. So we preferred to extend the discussion to clarify the matter. May Allah increase us in knowledge from His bounty; indeed He is the All-Knowing, the All-Knowing.

Then Exalted is He explains who among the relatives it is not obligatory to veil from, by His saying:

The discussion of the Lord's words, the Exalted:

[55] ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, the sons of their sisters, their women, or what their right hands possess. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness.﴾

﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, the sons of their sisters, or their women﴾ means: there is no sin or wrongdoing upon them in not veiling before these named persons. Al-Tabari said: By "their brothers and the sons of their brothers" is meant their brothers and the sons of their brothers, and the plural of these is included in that usage, just as the plural of fata (young man) is fityan. Thus the plural of akh (brother) when made plural is ikhwan. As for when it is made plural as ikhwa, that is like the plural of fata when made fitya.

**Remarks (tanbihat):**

**First:** It has been said that the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle are not mentioned because they are in the position of the parents. For this reason the paternal uncle is also called "father" in the words of the Exalted: ﴿the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:133]. Or it is because He dispensed with mentioning them by mentioning the sons of brothers and the sons of sisters, for the basis of the non-obligation of veiling between them and both groups is the very same relationship that exists between them and the paternal and maternal uncles, namely kinship through the paternal and maternal lines; since they are paternal aunts to the sons of brothers and maternal aunts to the sons of sisters. It has also been said: he disliked that they leave off veiling before them both, out of fear that they might describe them to their sons.

This is the view of Ikrimah and al-Sha'bi, as related by al-Tabari through the chain of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah and al-Sha'bi, that he said to them both: What is the matter with the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle that they were not mentioned? They both said: Because they describe them to their sons, and they disliked that she should remove her head-covering in front of her maternal uncle and paternal uncle.

Al-Shihab (al-Alusi) said: But this has been objected to, for this reason, namely the possibility that they might describe them to their sons, while they are permitted to marry them, applies to all women who are not mahram mothers (a mahram being one whom marriage to is forbidden permanently). Therefore one should rely on the first explanation. End of quote.

The verification in refuting this view is what al-Bukhari related in his Tafsir (exegesis) through the chain of Urwa, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Aflah, the brother of Abu al-Qu'ays, asked permission to enter upon me after the veiling had been revealed. I said: I will not permit him until I seek the permission of the Prophet ﷺ regarding him. For his brother Abu al-Qu'ays was not the one who nursed me; rather, it was the wife of Abu al-Qu'ays who nursed me. Then the Prophet ﷺ entered upon me, and I said to him: O Messenger of Allah! Aflah, the brother of Abu al-Qu'ays, asked permission, and I refused to permit him until I sought your permission. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'What prevented you from allowing him in? He is your paternal uncle.' I said: O Messenger of Allah! The man was not the one who nursed me; rather, it was the wife of Abu al-Qu'ays who nursed me. He said: 'Let him in, for he is your paternal uncle; may your right hand be dust-covered.'"

Urwa said: For this reason Aisha used to say: "Make unlawful through nursing what you make unlawful through lineage." End of quote. By his ﷺ saying, "Let him in, for he is your paternal uncle," together with his saying in another hadith, "The paternal uncle is the counterpart of the father," the matter is refuted against Ikrimah and al-Sha'bi.

**Second:** It has been said that by the words of the Exalted ﴿nor their women﴾ is meant Muslim women, so that it is not permissible for non-Muslim women (kitabiyyat, women of the People of the Book) to enter upon the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It has also been said that it is general, covering both Muslim women and women of the People of the Book. The phrase ﴿nor their women﴾ was used because they are of their own kind.

**Third:** Whoever held that a woman's slave is a mahram for her has cited the generality of the words of the Exalted ﴿nor what their right hands possess﴾. Others held that he is like the non-relatives (ajanib). The verse is specific to female slaves (ima') and not male slaves (abid), and the detailed explanation of this has already been given in Surah al-Nur.

**Fourth:** Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: al-Hasan and al-Husayn used the fact that the sons of paternal cousins are not mentioned in it as evidence for the prohibition of looking at them (the women), so they would not enter upon them. ﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is: that you transgress what is prescribed for you, so that you display of your adornment what is not permitted for you, or abandon the veil so that someone other than these persons sees you. Al-Razi said: That is, fear Him in the presence of the slaves. He said: In this is evidence that unveiling before them is conditional upon safety and knowing that no harm will result.

The words of the Exalted ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾ mean: He is Witness over what you do of veiling yourselves and of leaving off the veil before those before whom you are permitted to leave it off, and over your other affairs. So beware of meeting Him while He is a Witness against you for disobeying Him and for opposing His command and prohibition, and you perish. Al-Razi said: This closing reminder is most fitting in this place, because what preceded was an indication of the permissibility of being alone with them and unveiling before them. So He said: Indeed Allah is a witness when some of you are alone with others, so your privacy is like your public presence, with the witnessing of Allah, the Exalted; so be mindful of Him. End of quote.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying:

[56] ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace.﴾ al-Razi said: When Allah commanded the believers to seek permission (before entering) and not to gaze at the faces of his wives, out of reverence, He then completed the explanation of his sanctity. This is because his state is confined to two conditions: the condition of his solitude, which He indicated with the reverence due to him in that state through His saying, ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], and the condition in which he is in a gathering. A gathering is either the exalted gathering (al-mala' al-a'la) or the lower gathering (al-mala' al-adna). In the exalted gathering he is honored, for Allah and His angels send blessings upon him. As for the lower gathering, reverence toward him is obligatory, by the Exalted's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace.﴾ End of quotation.

Al-Bukhari transmitted from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: The blessing of Allah (salat Allah) is His praise of him in the presence of the angels, and the blessing of the angels is supplication. Ibn 'Abbas said: "yusallun" means "yubarrikun," i.e., they ask for blessing for him. This agrees with the saying of Abu al-'Aliyah, but it is more specific than it. In sum, salat carries the meanings of glorification, supplication and mercy, according to what it is attributed to in the Revelation or in the transmitted reports. The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim has expanded on the discussion of the meaning of salat in *Jala' al-Afham*, extensively and beneficially. So let it be consulted.

In al-Bukhari, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that: "It was said: O Messenger of Allah! As for the greeting of peace upon you, we already know it; so how is the blessing upon you (to be made)? He said: 'Say: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'"

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim in his *Mustadrak* transmitted from Abu Mas'ud al-Badri that: "They said: O Messenger of Allah! As for the greeting of peace, we already know it. So how should we send blessings upon you when we pray in our prayer? He said: 'Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad.'" And he mentioned it [the rest]. Al-Shafi'i transmitted it in his *Musnad* from Abu Hurayrah with the same meaning.

From here, al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that it is obligatory for the one praying to send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the final tashahhud. If he omits it, his prayer is not valid. Ahmad agreed with him in one narration. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and the Imam Ibn al-Mawwaz al-Maliki, among others, also said this, as Ibn al-Qayyim expounded in *Jala' al-Afham* and Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir*. Both of them, may mercy be upon them both, have thoroughly traced the narrations concerning the command to send blessings and its manner, and they gave it full treatment. So let them both be referred to.

**Remarks:**

**First:** The verse indicates that sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) is obligatory in general, because the basic principle in a command is obligation. Some held that it is obligatory once in a gathering, and then not obligatory for the rest of that gathering. [Others held] that it is obligatory once in one's lifetime, and then it is recommended in every circumstance. Others held that it is obligatory whenever he is mentioned. Some held that the verse indicates recommendation. Ibn Kathir said: This is a rare opinion, for the command to send blessings upon him has come at many times; some of them are obligatory and some recommended, as we will explain:

Among them is after the call to prayer (adhan), based on the hadith: "When you hear the muezzin, say what he says, then send blessings upon me," and the hadith continues.

Among them is upon entering the mosque, based on the hadith: "When he (ﷺ) entered the mosque, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: 'O Allah, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he left, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: 'O Allah, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your bounty.'"

Among them is the prayer itself: according to al-Shafi'i it is recommended in the first tashahhud, and obligatory in the second.

Among them is in the funeral prayer after the second takbir, following the saying of Abu Umamah: "It is from the Sunnah." This, from a Companion, has the ruling of a marfu' report, according to the correct view.

Among them is the conclusion of supplication, so sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in it is recommended, and the most emphatic of this is the supplication of qunut.

Among them is Friday and its night, so it is recommended to increase it on both. Among them is in the Friday sermon: it is obligatory for the preacher to include it in the two sermons. This is the position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Among them is when visiting his grave (ﷺ), based on the hadith: "No one greets me except that Allah returns my spirit to me until I return his greeting of peace." Abu Dawud alone transmitted it, and al-Nawawi authenticated it in *al-Adhkar*. From al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, that he saw people at the grave and forbade them, and said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do not take my grave as a festival, nor make your houses graves, and send blessings upon me wherever you are, for your blessings reach me.'"

Ibn Kathir said: Perhaps he saw them behaving discourteously by raising their voices beyond need, so he forbade them. It is also related that he saw a man frequenting the grave, and said: "O man! You and a man in al-Andalus are no different from each other"; i.e., all of them convey to him the blessings and peace of Allah upon him, constantly, until the Day of Judgment. The People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) have recommended that the scribe repeat the blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ) whenever he writes his name. It has been related in a hadith: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the blessing will continue to be written for him as long as my name is in that book."

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: This hadith is not authentic. Rather, the Hafiz al-Dhahabi counted it as fabricated (mawdu'). Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi mentioned that he saw in the handwriting of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, that he often wrote the name of the Prophet (ﷺ) without writing the blessing upon him. He said: "And it reached me that he used to send blessings upon him verbally."

**Second:** Sending blessings upon other than the prophets: if it is by way of following (tab'iyyah), like saying, "O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family and his wives," this is permissible by consensus (ijma'). As for doing it independently, some permitted it, based on the verse: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43], and the verse: ﴿Upon them are blessings from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 157], and the verse: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103], and the hadith: "When people came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with their charity, he would say: 'O Allah, bless them.' Then Abu Awfa came to him with his charity, and he said: 'O Allah, bless the family of Abu Awfa.'"

Others disliked it, because the formula of blessing (salat) became a distinctive mark (shi'ar) of the prophets when they are mentioned, so it is not to be extended to others. Thus one does not say, "Umar said, may Allah bless him," just as one does not say, "Muhammad, Mighty and Majestic," even though he is mighty and majestic; because this is part of the distinctive mark of the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They interpreted what came in the Book and the Sunnah in this regard as supplication for them.

Ibn Hajar said: This occurred from the Lawgiver (al-Shari'), and the one who has a right may waive of his right as he wishes, and no one else may dispose of it except with his permission; and no permission from him concerning this has been established. End of quotation.

And it may be said: The transmitted report cited above suffices as permission. Arguing that it is a matter of his right begs the question (musadarah 'ala al-matlub). Furthermore, the preferred view is that the basic principle is permissibility until a prohibition is established, and there is no prohibition here. So reflect.

As for the greeting of peace (salam), al-Juwayni said: It has the meaning of salat, so it is not used for an absent person, and it is not singled out for anyone other than the prophets; so one does not say, "Ali, peace be upon him." This applies equally to the living and the dead. As for one present, he is addressed with it, so one says, "Peace be upon you" (salam 'alayka), or "Peace be upon you all" (salam 'alaykum), or "Peace be upon you" (al-salam 'alayka or 'alaykum). It has become prevalent, as Ibn Kathir said, among many copyists of books, to single out Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, by writing, "peace be upon him" (alayhi al-salam), to the exclusion of the rest of the Companions. He said: Equalizing them in this matter is better. End of quotation.

The matter is easy. Whoever sees what is transmitted on this subject knows that the matter is broader than to be made a hardship. Moreover, this question is among the branches of the specification by custom ('urf), and there is a discussion of it in the principles of jurisprudence (usul).

**Third:** Al-Nawawi said: When one sends blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he should combine the blessing and the greeting of peace, and not limit himself to one of them. So he should not say only "Allah bless him," nor only "peace be upon him."

Ibn Kathir said: What al-Nawawi said is derived from this noble verse: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace.﴾ So the better form is to say, "(ﷺ)" with the greeting of peace.

End of quotation.

**Fourth:** Al-Razi said: If Allah and His angels send blessings upon him, what need is there for our blessings? We say: Sending blessings upon him is not because he needs them. Otherwise, there would be no need for the angels' blessings alongside Allah's blessing upon him. Rather, it is to manifest his exaltation, just as Allah the Exalted obligated us to mention Himself, while He has no need of it; it is only to manifest our exaltation of Him, as mercy toward us, so that He rewards us for it. Therefore it has come in the hadith: "Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings upon him ten times for it." End of quotation.

A few days ago I had written in the introduction to a collection of sermons on the secret of sending blessings upon him something similar to this: "It is recommended on Friday to increase sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), so that one may recall the mercy of his mission, the grace of his guidance, the favor of following his way and Sunnah, the greatest righteousness through his message, striving for the truth through his conduct, the noble morals through his wisdom, and the happiness of both abodes through his call (ﷺ), and upon his family, for no seeker has tasted the secret of his law, nor has the light of truth shone upon his insight, so that he is happy in this world and the next."

**Fifth:** Al-Razi said: He mentioned "taslimah" (fully) for emphasis, so that the greeting of peace upon him is completed, and He did not emphasize the blessing with this emphasis, because it was already emphasized by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet.﴾ End of quotation.

It has been said: This is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device of omission in which each clause omits what the other states). So "upon him" (alayhi) is omitted from one of the two, and the verbal noun (al-masdar) is omitted from the other.

The judge (al-Qadi) said: It has been said that the meaning of ﴿and greet him with the greeting of peace﴾ is: submit to his commands. So "salam" comes from "taslim" and submission.

**Sixth:** The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*: I was asked about attributing the blessing to Allah without the greeting of peace, and about the command to the believers to do both. I said: It may be that salam has two meanings: greeting (tahiyyah) and submission (inqiyad). So the believers were commanded to do it, since both are valid from them. Allah and His angels cannot submit, so it is not attributed to them, to avoid ambiguity. And knowledge is with Allah. End of quotation.

Al-Shihab said: There has appeared to me a secret point concerning the specification of the greeting of peace to the believers without Allah and His angels: that the greeting of peace means guarding him from what harms him. When this verse came right after the mention of what harms the Prophet (ﷺ), and harm comes only from humans, and it had come from them, the specification to them and the emphasis were fitting. End of quotation. And when the Exalted commanded the blessing upon His Prophet (ﷺ), which is praise of him, glorification and exaltation, He made a threat against the one who does not observe it, by daring to oppose it, with His saying, Glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[57] ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ That is, they will receive disgrace and ignominy because of it. The intended referent of the verse is the Messenger (ﷺ), and the mention of Allah the Exalted is only to magnify him, by showing his nearness to Allah and that he is His beloved, so that whatever harms him is as if it harms Allah, just as whoever obeys him obeys Allah. Al-Tabari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning those who slandered the Prophet (ﷺ) when he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. In reality, this is one of the instances covered by the verse. Indeed, if it were said that it refers to those who engaged in the matter of Zaynab, it would be closer, because of the closeness of the verses in this theme and their coherence as a single chain, concerning that matter which was the greatest purpose of the entire surah, as is not hidden from one who reflects upon it.

In sum, the wording is general to every kind of harm that befalls him (ﷺ), so the intended object of the revelation enters it primarily. On this basis, "harming" (al-adhiyyah) is in its literal sense. It has also been said that the meaning of harming Allah and His Messenger is committing what they do not approve of, as a metonymy (majaz mursal, an unrestricted figurative usage) because it is a cause of, or necessarily connected to, the harm; and although it is in relation to others, it is in the sense of the connection, while the mention of Allah and His Messenger is in its apparent sense. Whoever permits the use of a single word in two meanings, as in using a homonym (lafz mushtarak) in both its meanings, or in both its literal and figurative senses, interprets "harming" in both meanings according to the two objects of the verb: thus, with respect to Allah the Exalted, it means committing what is disliked, figuratively, and with respect to the Messenger, it is in its apparent sense. For the multiplicity of the object is equivalent to the repetition of the governing verb, so the combining of both meanings applies to it.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[58] ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women for what they have not earned have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾

﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women﴾, i.e., by speech or by action. ﴿For what they have not earned﴾, i.e., without any offense that would deserve harm. ﴿Then they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾, i.e., clear and evident.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He made the harming of Allah and His Messenger absolute, and restricted the harming of believing men and women, because the harm done to Allah and His Messenger is never anything but unjust, whereas harm done to believing men and women may be just or unjust.

**Note (tanbih):** In *al-Iklil*: This verse prohibits harming a Muslim except by a legitimate cause, such as punishing him for a sin. Included in the verse is everything that is forbidden because it causes harm, such as selling over another's sale, bidding over another's bid, and proposing over another's proposal. Al-Shafi'i explicitly stated the prohibition of a person eating from what is placed in front of another when that involves causing harm. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from the hadith of 'Aisha, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The most usurious of usury in the sight of Allah is the violation of the honor of a Muslim person," and then he recited this verse. He also transmitted from Qatada regarding this verse: "Beware of harming the believer, for Allah protects him and becomes angry on his behalf." It is alleged that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited it one day, and it frightened him, so he went to Ubayy ibn Ka'b and entered upon him and said: "O Abu al-Mundhir! I recited a verse from the Book of Allah and it struck me in every way: ﴿And those who harm believing men﴾ [to the end of the verse]. By Allah, I will punish them and beat them." He said to him: "You are not one of them. You are only a disciplinarian; you are only a teacher." End.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was also reported from al-Fudayl: "It is not lawful for you to harm a dog or a pig without right, so how about a human being?" Ibn 'Awn would not rent out shops except to people of the dhimma (protected non-Muslims), because of the fear of being harmed by them when the year turns over. May Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him.

When Allah, exalted is He, explained the evil condition of those who harm, as a deterrent for them from harming, He commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to instruct some of those who are harmed by them with what would generally repel their harm, through concealment and distinction from the places of harm, by His saying, glory be to Him:

(p-4908) The explanation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[59] ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments (jalabib) close around them. That is more suitable so that they will be recognized and not be harmed. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments close around them﴾: *jalabib* is the plural of *jilbab* (on the pattern of *sirdab*), which is a wrap worn over the *khimar* (headcover) with which a woman covers herself. This is the meaning of some people's saying: "Her *jilbab* is her wrapper with which she wraps herself." It was also said that it is the *khimar*. Janub, the sister of Amr dhu al-Kalb, said in his elegy:

"The vultures walk toward him, unconcerned, with the gait of young virgins, over whom are *jalalib*."

Another poet, describing grey hair, said:

"Until the head was clothed in a grey covering, the most hateful *jilbab* for one who wears it."

Al-Zamakhshari said: The *jilbab* is a wide garment, wider than the *khimar* and less than the *rida'* (mantle). The woman wraps it around her head, and what remains of it she lets fall over her chest. It is reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it is the *rida'* that covers from above to below. Then he said: The meaning of "let them draw their outer garments close around them" is that they let them down over themselves and cover with them their faces and their sides. It is said, when a woman's covering slips from her face: "Pull your garment over your face." That is because in the early days of Islam women were, in their pre-Islamic ignorance, accustomed to going about in undress: a woman would go out in a shift and a headcover, with no distinction between free woman and slave. Young men and those given to mischief would accost slave women when they went out at night to attend to their needs among the palm groves and the fields; and sometimes they would approach a free woman under the pretext that she was a slave, saying, "We thought she was a slave." So they were commanded to differ in their dress from the dress of slave women, by wearing wraps and cloaks and covering their heads and faces, (p-4909) so that they would be modest and be respected, and no one who desires them would hope for them. This is His saying: ﴿That is more suitable so that they will be recognized and not be harmed﴾, meaning: more fitting and more deserving that they be recognized as free women, so that none will approach them and they will not encounter what they dislike. Then al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the meaning of *min* (from) in ﴿from their outer garments﴾? I say: it is partitive, but the partitive sense admits two interpretations:

First: that they wrap themselves with some of the outer garments they possess. The intended meaning is that a free woman should not go about in undress, in a shift and headcover, like a slave woman or a servant, and that she should have two or more *jilbab*s in her house.

Second: that a woman lets down part of her *jilbab* and its excess over her face, so that she veils herself and is distinguished from a slave woman. End of quotation.

Among the reports on this verse is what al-Tabari related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah commanded the women of the believers, when they went out of their houses for some need, to cover their faces from above their heads with the *jalabib*, and to show only one eye. Ibn Abi Hatim related from Umm Salamah, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿they draw their outer garments close around them﴾, the women of the Ansar came out as if there were crows upon their heads, out of tranquility, and they wore black cloaks. And he related from Yunus ibn Yazid that he asked al-Zuhri: Must a slave girl wear a *khimar*, whether she is married or not? He said: She must wear the *khimar* if she is married, and she is forbidden the *jilbab*, because it is disliked for them to resemble free, chaste women.

Remarks:

The first: Ibn Kathir said: It is reported from Sufyan al-Thawri that he said: There is no harm in looking at the adornment of the women of the People of the Covenant (dhimmis), and looking at them is forbidden only out of fear of temptation, not because of their sanctity. He cited in evidence His saying: ﴿and the women of the believers﴾. End of quotation.

The second: Al-Subki said in his *Tabaqat* (Tabaqat al-Shafi'iyya al-Kubra): Ahmad ibn Isa, one of the Shafi'i jurists, deduced from this verse that what the scholars and nobles do of changing their dress and turbans is a good thing, even if the early generation (al-salaf) did not do it, because in it there is a distinction for them so that they may be recognized and their words acted upon. End of quotation.

(p-4910) The third: Al-Shihab said: His saying ﴿they draw﴾ may be the object of the speech ("say"), and it is a report in the sense of a command, or an answer to a command, in the manner of: ﴿Tell My servants who believe to establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 31]. End of quotation. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾, meaning: for whatever of negligence has passed from them. ﴿Merciful﴾, meaning: toward His servants, in that He takes account of their interests, even down to the minutiae of them.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[60–61] "If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in the city, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little. Cursed; wherever they are found, they will be seized and slain with [intensive] slaughter."

"If the hypocrites do not desist" means: from their hypocrisy. "And those in whose hearts is a disease" means: weakness of faith, [and their] soliciting of women to immorality. "And the agitators in the city" means: those who spread and circulate news of evil, such as the arrival of an enemy or the defeat of a detachment, and similar things by which they break the hearts of the believers. Its root meaning is agitation, from "al-rajfah" (the quaking), which is tremor; the fabricated report is called by this name because it is a shaking, unstable report that is not firm, or because the hearts of the believers are agitated by it. "We will surely incite you against them" means: We will surely give you power over them with that which compels them to exile. "Then they will not remain your neighbors therein" means: in the city, because of the strength of your might against them. "Except for a little" means: for a brief time, while they prepare for departure. "Cursed; wherever they are found" means: hated by Allah and by creation, unable to find rest by leaving, because the curse clings to them wherever they are found. "They will be seized and slain with [intensive] slaughter" means: they will be taken captive, and their killing will be emphasized because of their humiliation and their scarcity. Then the Exalted indicated that this is not something novel, by His saying:
